sentences.zh: 柳元景

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing

sentences.zh: 柳元景字孝仁，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing, styled Xiaoren, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing, whose courtesy name was Xiaoren, came from Jie in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖卓，自本郡遷於襄陽，官至汝南太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhuo moved from his native commandery to Xiangyang and reached the office of Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhuo had left his home commandery for Xiangyang and eventually served as administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖恬，西河太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tian was Administrator of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian held the post of Xihe administrator.

sentences.zh: 父憑，馮翊太守。

translations.literal: His father Ping was Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ping served as Fengyi administrator.

sentences.zh: 元景少便弓馬，數隨父伐蠻，以勇稱。

translations.literal: Yuanjing from youth was skilled with bow and horse; he often followed his father in campaigns against the Man and was famed for courage.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yuanjing was adept with bow and horse. He often accompanied his father on campaigns against the southern tribes and won a reputation for bravery.

sentences.zh: 寡言有器質。

translations.literal: He spoke little and possessed substantial character.
translations.idiomatic: He was sparing of speech and showed real capacity.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史謝晦聞其名，要之，未及往而晦敗。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Inspector Xie Hui heard his name and summoned him, but before he could go, Hui was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, inspector of Jingzhou, heard of him and invited him to serve, but Yuanjing had not yet gone when Hui fell.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史劉道產深愛其能，元景時居父憂，未得加命。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector Liu Daochan deeply admired his ability, but Yuanjing was then in mourning for his father and could not yet receive an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daochan, inspector of Yongzhou, greatly valued his talent, yet Yuanjing was still in mourning for his father and could not yet be given office.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史江夏王義恭召之，道產謂曰：「久欲見屈。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou Inspector Prince Jiangxia Yigong summoned him, Daochan said to him, "For a long time I have wished to detain you.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jiangxia of Jiangxia, as inspector of Jingzhou, summoned him, Daochan said, "I have long wanted to keep you here.

sentences.zh: 今貴王有召，難輒相留，乖意以為惘惘。」

translations.literal: Now the honored prince has summoned you; it is hard to detain you at once—against my wish I feel regretful."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the prince has called you, I cannot simply hold you back, and against my wishes I am left deeply disappointed."

sentences.zh: 服闋，補江夏王國中軍將軍，遷殿中將軍。

translations.literal: When his mourning ended, he was appointed Central Army General of the Jiangxia princedom and was promoted to Palace General.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was over, he was made central army general of the Jiangxia princedom and then promoted to palace general.

sentences.zh: 復為義恭司空行參軍，隨府轉司徒太尉城局參軍，太祖見又嘉之。

translations.literal: He again served Yigong as acting aide on the staff of the Minister of Works; following the princedom he became an aide in the city bureau of the Minister over the Masses and Grand Marshal, and the Taizu saw him and again praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He again served Yigong as acting staff officer on the Minister of Works' secretariat, then followed the establishment to a post in the city bureau of the Minister over the Masses and Grand Marshal. The Taizu saw him once more and commended him.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉道產在雍州有惠化，遠蠻悉歸懷，皆出緣沔為村落，戶口殷盛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Daochan in Yongzhou had benevolent governance; distant Man all submitted in heart, all coming out along the Han to form villages, and the population was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Liu Daochan governed Yongzhou, his benevolent rule had won over the distant tribes. They settled in villages along the Han River, and the population grew thick.

sentences.zh: 及道產死，羣蠻大為寇暴。

translations.literal: When Daochan died, the Man tribes greatly raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: After Daochan's death, the tribal peoples launched major raids.

sentences.zh: 世祖西鎮襄陽，義恭以元景為將帥，即以為廣威將軍、隨郡太守。

translations.literal: The Shizu garrisoned the west at Xiangyang; Yigong made Yuanjing a commander and at once appointed him General of Expansive Might and Administrator of Suixian.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu held the western garrison at Xiangyang. Yigong chose Yuanjing as a field commander and immediately made him general of expansive might and administrator of Suixian commandery.

sentences.zh: 既至，而蠻斷驛道，欲來攻郡。

translations.literal: When he had arrived, the Man cut the post road and intended to come attack the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived, the tribes cut the courier road and prepared to attack the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 郡內少糧，器仗又乏，元景設方略，得六七百人，分五百人屯驛道。

translations.literal: Within the commandery grain was scant and weapons too were lacking; Yuanjing devised a plan and mustered six or seven hundred men, dividing five hundred to garrison the post road.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had little grain and few arms. Yuanjing worked out a plan, raised six or seven hundred men, and sent five hundred to hold the post road.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「蠻將逼城，不宜分眾。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "The Man will soon press the city; it is not fitting to divide the force."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him, "The tribes are about to threaten the city—you should not split your force."

sentences.zh: 元景曰：「蠻聞郡遣重戍，豈悟城內兵少。

translations.literal: Yuanjing said, "When the Man hear the commandery has sent a heavy garrison, how would they realize the troops in the city are few?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing replied, "When the tribes hear that the commandery has sent a strong detachment, how will they guess how few men remain inside the walls?

sentences.zh: 且表裏合攻，於計為長。」

translations.literal: Moreover, attacking together from without and within is the superior plan."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, striking them from front and rear at once is the better strategy."

sentences.zh: 會蠻垂至，乃使驛道為備，潛出其後，戒曰：「火舉馳進。」

translations.literal: When the Man were about to arrive, he had the post-road force make ready while he secretly came out behind them, instructing, "When the signal fire is raised, charge forward."
translations.idiomatic: As the tribes drew near, he had the men on the post road stand ready while he slipped around behind them with orders: "When you see the beacon, ride hard."

sentences.zh: 前後俱發，蠻眾驚擾，投鄖水死者千餘人，斬獲數百，郡境肅然，無復寇抄。

translations.literal: Front and rear both struck; the Man masses were thrown into panic, and more than a thousand who plunged into the Yun River died; several hundred were beheaded or captured, and within the commandery all was quiet with no further raids.
translations.idiomatic: Both wings struck at once. The tribal force broke in panic; more than a thousand drowned in the Yun River, and several hundred were killed or taken. The commandery grew calm, and raiding ceased.

sentences.zh: 朱脩之討蠻，元景又與之俱，後又副沈慶之征鄖山，進克太陽。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xiuzhi campaigned against the Man, Yuanjing again went with him; later he served as deputy to Shen Qingzhi in the campaign against Mount Yun and advanced to take Taiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xiuzhi campaigned against the tribes, Yuanjing marched with him again. Later he served under Shen Qingzhi against Mount Yun and helped capture Taiyang.

sentences.zh: 除世祖安北府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Central Troops Aide in the Shizu's Pacify-the-North headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was made central troops aide on the Shizu's Pacify-the-North staff.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕鎮襄陽，為後軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Sui Dan garrisoned Xiangyang, Yuanjing served as Central Troops Aide of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sui Dan held Xiangyang, Yuanjing became central troops aide of the rear army on his staff.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷大舉北討，使諸鎮各出軍。

translations.literal: When the court launched a great northern campaign, it ordered each garrison to send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the court mounted a major northern expedition, every regional command was told to deploy its forces.

sentences.zh: 二十七年八月，誕遣振威將軍尹顯祖出貲谷，奮武將軍魯方平、建武將軍薛安都、略陽太守龐法起入盧氏，廣威將軍田義仁入魯陽，加元景建威將軍，總統羣帥。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year twenty-seven, Dan sent Quelling Might General Yin Xianzu out through Zigui Valley, Striving Martial General Lu Fangping, Establishing Martial General Xue Andu, and Administrator of Lueyang Pang Faqi into Lushi, and Expansive Might General Tian Yiren into Luyang; Yuanjing was promoted to Establishing Might General and given overall command of the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 27, Dan sent Quelling Might General Yin Xianzu through Zigui Valley, Striving Martial General Lu Fangping, Establishing Martial General Xue Andu, and Lueyang administrator Pang Faqi into Lushi, while Expansive Might General Tian Yiren advanced on Luyang. Yuanjing was promoted to establishing might general and placed in overall command of the field leaders.

sentences.zh: 後軍外兵參軍龐季明年已七十三，秦之冠族，羌人多附之，求入長安，招懷關、陝。

translations.literal: Rear Army Outer Troops Aide Pang Jiming was already seventy-three, a leading clan of Qin; many Qiang attached to him. He asked to enter Chang'an and win over Guanzhong and the Shaan region.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jiming, outer troops aide of the rear army, was already seventy-three—a great Qin clan chief to whom many Qiang looked. He volunteered to enter Chang'an and rally Guanzhong and western Shaan.

sentences.zh: 乃自貲谷入盧氏，盧氏人趙難納之，弘農強門先有內附意，故委季明投之。

translations.literal: He then entered Lushi from Zigui Valley; Zhao Nan of Lushi received him. Powerful families of Hongnong had long wished to submit inward, so they entrusted Jiming to them.
translations.idiomatic: He came into Lushi from Zigui Valley, where Zhao Nan of Lushi welcomed him. Leading families in Hongnong had already leaned toward submission, so they put themselves under Jiming's lead.

sentences.zh: 十月，魯方平、薛安都、龐法起進次白亭，時元景猶未發。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Lu Fangping, Xue Andu, and Pang Faqi advanced and halted at Baiting; at that time Yuanjing had still not set out.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Lu Fangping, Xue Andu, and Pang Faqi marched up to Baiting, while Yuanjing had not yet moved.

sentences.zh: 法起率方平、安都諸軍前入，自脩陽亭出熊耳山。

translations.literal: Faqi led Fangping, Andu, and the other armies forward, going out from Xiuyang Pavilion through Bear's-Ear Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi led Fangping, Andu, and the rest forward, leaving Xiuyang Pavilion by way of Bear's-Ear Mountain.

sentences.zh: 季明進達高門木城，值永昌王入弘農，乃回，還盧氏，據險自固。

translations.literal: Jiming advanced to Gaomen Wooden Fort; he encountered Prince Yongchang entering Hongnong, then turned back, returned to Lushi, and held the defiles to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming reached Gaomen Wooden Fort just as Prince Yongchang entered Hongnong. He withdrew to Lushi and fortified the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 頃之，招盧氏少年進入宜陽苟公谷，以扇動義心。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he recruited young men of Lushi to enter Gougong Valley in Yiyang to stir up loyal sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he rallied Lushi youths into Gougong Valley in Yiyang to rouse local loyalists.

sentences.zh: 元景以其月率軍繼進。

translations.literal: In that same month Yuanjing led the army in continued advance.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Yuanjing marched up with the main army.

sentences.zh: 閏月，法起、安都、方平諸軍入盧氏，斬縣令李封，以趙難為盧氏令，加奮武將軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, the armies of Faqi, Andu, and Fangping entered Lushi, beheaded Magistrate Li Feng, made Zhao Nan magistrate of Lushi, and promoted him to Striving Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Faqi, Andu, and Fangping took Lushi, executed Magistrate Li Feng, appointed Zhao Nan magistrate of Lushi, and gave him the rank of striving martial general.

sentences.zh: 難驅率義徒，以為眾軍鄉導。

translations.literal: Nan drove the loyal volunteers and served as guide for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Nan led the local volunteers and guided the allied columns.

sentences.zh: 法起等度鐵嶺山，次開方口，季明出自木城，與法起相會。

translations.literal: Faqi and the others crossed Iron Ridge Mountain and halted at Kaifang Pass; Jiming came out from Wooden Fort and joined Faqi.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi's force crossed Iron Ridge Mountain and camped at Kaifang Pass. Jiming came out of Wooden Fort and linked up with him.

sentences.zh: 元景大軍次臼口，以前鋒深入，懸軍無繼，馳遣尹顯祖入盧氏，以為軍援。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's great army halted at Jiukou; because the vanguard had penetrated deep and the army hung forward without follow-up, he urgently sent Yin Xianzu into Lushi as military reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing's main force stopped at Jiukou. With the vanguard far ahead and no reserves behind it, he hurried Yin Xianzu into Lushi as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 元景以軍食不足，難可曠日相持，乃束馬懸車，引軍上百丈崖，出溫谷，以入盧氏。

translations.literal: Yuanjing, because army provisions were insufficient and a prolonged standoff was hard to sustain, bound horses and suspended carts, led the army up Hundred-Foot Cliff, came out through Warm Valley, and entered Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were short and a long stalemate was impossible, so Yuanjing had horses packed and wagons winched up Hundred-Foot Cliff, then led his men through Warm Valley into Lushi.

sentences.zh: 法起諸軍進次方伯堆，去弘農城五里。

translations.literal: Faqi's armies advanced and halted at Fangbo Mound, five li from Hongnong city.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi's columns marched up to Fangbo Mound, five li from the walls of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 賊遣兵二千餘人覘候，法起縱兵夾射之，賊騎退走。

translations.literal: The enemy sent more than two thousand men to reconnoiter; Faqi loosed troops to shoot at them from both sides, and the enemy horsemen fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent out more than two thousand scouts. Faqi attacked them from both flanks with archery, and their cavalry broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 諸軍造攻具，進兵城下，偽弘農太守李初古拔嬰城自固，法起、安都、方平諸軍鼓譟以陵城，季明、趙難並率義徒相繼而進，衝車四臨，數道俱攻，士皆殊死戰，莫不奮勇爭先。

translations.literal: The armies built siege engines and advanced to the foot of the wall. The false Administrator of Hongnong Li Chuguba shut the city and held firm. The armies of Faqi, Andu, and Fangping drummed and clamored to storm the wall; Jiming and Zhao Nan both led loyal volunteers forward in succession; battering rams pressed on four sides and several routes attacked together; the soldiers all fought to the death, none failing to strive forward in courage.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies built siege engines and moved to the walls. The Wei-appointed Hongnong administrator Li Chuguba barred the gates and held on. Faqi, Andu, and Fangping raised a thunder of drums beneath the ramparts while Jiming and Zhao Nan pushed volunteer columns forward. Battering rams closed in on four sides and assault parties struck along several approaches. Every man fought as if for his life, each striving to be first.

sentences.zh: 時初古拔父子據南門，督其處距戰，弘農人之在城內者三千餘人，於北樓豎白幡，或射無金箭。

translations.literal: At that time Chuguba and his son held the south gate and directed the defense there. More than three thousand people of Hongnong inside the city raised white banners on the north tower or shot arrows without metal heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chuguba and his son manned the south gate and directed the defense. More than three thousand Hongnong residents inside the city raised white banners on the north tower or shot signal arrows without iron points.

sentences.zh: 安都軍副譚金、薛係孝率眾先登，生禽李初古拔父子二人，魯方平入南門，生禽偽郡丞，百姓皆安堵。

translations.literal: Andu's army deputies Tan Jin and Xue Xixiao led the troops to scale first and took Li Chuguba and his son alive. Lu Fangping entered the south gate and took the false commandery aide alive; the common people all settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Andu's deputies Tan Jin and Xue Xixiao led the assault and captured Li Chuguba and his son alive. Lu Fangping entered the south gate and seized the Wei commandery aide. The townspeople were left unmolested.

sentences.zh: 元景引軍度熊耳山，安都頓軍弘農，法起進據潼關，季明率方平、趙難軍向陝西七里谷。

translations.literal: Yuanjing led the army across Bear's-Ear Mountain; Andu encamped at Hongnong; Faqi advanced to hold Tong Pass; Jiming led the armies of Fangping and Zhao Nan toward Qili Valley west of Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing crossed Bear's-Ear Mountain while Andu encamped at Hongnong, Faqi seized Tong Pass, and Jiming marched Fangping and Zhao Nan toward Qili Valley west of Shaan.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍鄧盛、幢主劉驂亂使人入荒田，招宜陽人劉寬虯率合義徒二千餘人，共攻金門隖，屠之。

translations.literal: Palace General Deng Sheng and standard-bearer Liu Canluan sent men into Huangtian to recruit Liu Kuangqiu of Yiyang, who gathered more than two thousand loyal volunteers; together they attacked Jintun Fort and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace general Deng Sheng and standard-bearer Liu Canluan sent agents into Huangtian to rally Liu Kuangqiu of Yiyang, who mustered more than two thousand volunteers. Together they stormed Jintun Fort and put its garrison to the sword.

sentences.zh: 殺戍主李買得，古拔子也，為虜永昌王長史，勇冠戎類。

translations.literal: They killed the garrison commander Li Maide, son of Chuguba, who was chief clerk to the enemy Prince Yongchang and whose courage topped the barbarian ranks.
translations.idiomatic: They killed the garrison commander Li Maide—Chuguba's son—who served as chief clerk to Prince Yongchang and was counted the bravest man in the Wei armies.

sentences.zh: 永昌聞其死，若失左右手。

translations.literal: When Yongchang heard of his death, it was as if he had lost both arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongchang heard that Maide was dead, he felt as though he had lost both hands.

sentences.zh: 誕又遣長流行參軍姚範領三千人向弘農，受元景節度。

translations.literal: Dan again sent Chief Clerk Aide Yao Fan leading three thousand men toward Hongnong, subject to Yuanjing's command.
translations.idiomatic: Dan also sent chief clerk aide Yao Fan with three thousand men toward Hongnong under Yuanjing's orders.

sentences.zh: 十一月，元景率眾至弘農，營於開方口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yuanjing led the masses to Hongnong and encamped at Kaifang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yuanjing brought his main force to Hongnong and pitched camp at Kaifang Pass.

sentences.zh: 仍以元景為弘農太守，置吏佐。

translations.literal: He was again made Yuanjing Administrator of Hongnong and staff officers were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was again appointed administrator of Hongnong, with a full staff of aides.

sentences.zh: 初，安都留住弘農，而諸軍已進陝，元景既到，謂安都曰：「無為坐守空城，而令龐公深入，此非計也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Andu had remained at Hongnong while the armies had already advanced on Shaan. When Yuanjing arrived, he said to Andu, "Do not sit guarding an empty city while letting Lord Pang press deep—this is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Andu had stayed behind at Hongnong while the other columns were already moving on Shaan. When Yuanjing arrived he told Andu, "You should not sit in an empty city while Pang pushes deep into enemy country—that is no strategy.

sentences.zh: 宜急進軍，可與顯祖并兵就之。

translations.literal: You should hurry the army forward; you may join forces with Xianzu and go to him.
translations.idiomatic: March at once. You can join Xianzu and go to his aid.

sentences.zh: 吾須督租畢，尋後引也。」

translations.literal: I must finish supervising the grain levy and will lead up afterward."
translations.idiomatic: I still have to finish collecting supplies and will follow shortly."

sentences.zh: 眾並造陝下，即入郭城，列營於城內以逼之，並大造攻具。

translations.literal: The forces all advanced to Shaan, entered the outer city at once, arrayed camps inside the wall to press the enemy, and on a large scale built siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: The columns all marched to Shaan, entered the outer city, and pitched camp inside the walls to tighten the siege while building siege engines on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 賊城臨河為固，恃險自守，季明、安都、方平、顯祖、趙難諸軍，頻三攻未拔。

translations.literal: The enemy city leaned on the river for defense and relied on the terrain to hold itself; the armies of Jiming, Andu, Fangping, Xianzu, and Zhao Nan attacked three times in succession without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held a river-side strongpoint and trusted the terrain. Jiming, Andu, Fangping, Xianzu, and Zhao Nan assaulted three times without breaking the place.

sentences.zh: 虜洛州刺史地河公張是連提眾二萬，度崤來救，安都、方平各列陣城南以待之，顯祖勒精卒以為後柱。

translations.literal: The enemy Luozhou Inspector Duke of Dihe Zhang Shilian brought twenty thousand men, crossed Xiao Mountain to rescue, and Andu and Fangping each drew up battle lines south of the city to await them; Xianzu led picked troops as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Luozhou inspector, Duke of Dihe Zhang Shilian, brought twenty thousand men over Xiao Mountain to relieve the city. Andu and Fangping formed battle lines south of the walls while Xianzu held picked troops in reserve.

sentences.zh: 季明率高明、宜陽義兵當南門而陣，趙難領盧氏樂從少年，與季明為掎角。

translations.literal: Jiming led the loyal troops of Gaoming and Yiyang to face the south gate in battle array; Zhao Nan led the willing youths of Lushi and formed pincers with Jiming.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming posted the volunteer forces of Gaoming and Yiyang before the south gate. Zhao Nan led the eager young men of Lushi to work a pincer with him.

sentences.zh: 賊兵大合，輕騎挑戰。

translations.literal: The enemy forces massed greatly and light cavalry offered challenge.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army gathered in force and sent light cavalry to provoke a fight.

sentences.zh: 安都瞋目橫矛，單騎突陣，四向奮擊，左右皆辟易不能當，殺傷不可勝數，於是眾軍並鼓噪俱前，士皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: Andu glared and levelled his spear, charging the formation alone on horseback, striking fiercely in four directions; those to left and right all gave way and could not withstand him, and the killed and wounded were beyond counting. Thereupon all armies drummed and clamored forward together, and the soldiers all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Andu glared, levelled his spear, and charged alone into the enemy line, striking in every direction. Men on either flank fell back before him, and the dead and wounded were beyond count. At that the whole allied army surged forward with a roar, every soldier fighting as if for his life.

sentences.zh: 虜初縱突騎，眾軍患之，安都怒甚，乃脫兜鍪，解所帶鎧，唯著絳納兩當衫，馬亦去具裝，馳奔以入賊陣，猛氣咆𠷺，所向無前，當其鋒者，無不應刃而倒。

translations.literal: At first the enemy loosed shock cavalry and the armies were troubled by it. Andu was extremely angry; he then removed his helmet, stripped the armor he wore, wore only a crimson cross-strap jacket, and his horse too shed full barding; he galloped into the enemy formation roaring, irresistible wherever he went—those who met his point all fell to the blade.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei first unleashed shock cavalry, and the allied ranks wavered. Andu flew into a rage, tore off his helmet and armor, and rode in wearing only a crimson jacket while his horse too was stripped of barding. He charged into the enemy roaring, and wherever he turned no one who met his spear failed to fall.

sentences.zh: 賊忿之，夾射不能中，如是者數四，每一入，眾無不披靡。

translations.literal: The enemy were enraged at him; they shot at him from both sides but could not hit him. This happened four or five times; each time he entered, the masses invariably broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy loosed volleys at him from both sides but could not bring him down. Four or five times he plunged in, and each time the Wei ranks broke before him.

sentences.zh: 初，元景令將魯元保守函谷關，賊眾既盛，元保不能自固，乃率所領作函箱陣，多列旗幟，緣險而還，正會安都諸軍與賊交戰，虜三郎將見元保軍從山下，以為元景大眾至，日且暮，賊於是奔退，騎多得入城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuanjing had ordered General Lu Yuanbao to hold Hangu Pass. When the enemy masses had grown strong, Yuanbao could not hold firm; he then led his command in a box formation, set out many banners and flags, and returned along the defiles—just as Andu's armies were engaging the enemy in battle. A Wei third-rank general saw Yuanbao's army coming down the mountain, thought Yuanjing's great host had arrived, and as the day was near dusk the enemy therefore fled in retreat; many horsemen were able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuanjing had posted General Lu Yuanbao to hold Hangu Pass. When Wei pressure grew too heavy Yuanbao could not hold the pass. He drew his men into a box formation, raised a forest of banners, and withdrew along the mountain paths—just as Andu was fighting below. A Wei third-rank officer saw Yuanbao's column coming down the slope, took it for Yuanjing's main army, and with dusk falling the enemy broke. Many of their horsemen escaped into the city.

sentences.zh: 賊之將至也，方平遣驛騎告元景，時諸軍糧盡，各餘數日食。

translations.literal: When the enemy were about to arrive, Fangping sent a post courier to inform Yuanjing; at that time the armies' grain was exhausted and each had only several days' food left.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy relief force approached, Fangping sent a courier to Yuanjing. Every column was out of grain and had only a few days' rations left.

sentences.zh: 元景方督義租，并上驢馬，以為運糧之計，而方平信至，元景遣軍副柳元怙簡步騎二千，以赴陝急。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was then supervising the loyal grain levy and also requisitioning donkeys and horses for a transport plan, but when Fangping's letter arrived, Yuanjing sent army deputy Liu Yuanhu to select two thousand foot and horse to hurry to Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was busy collecting grain and rounding up pack animals when Fangping's message arrived. He sent his deputy Liu Yuanhu with two thousand picked infantry and cavalry to relieve Shaan at once.

sentences.zh: 卷甲兼行，一宿而至。

translations.literal: They rolled up armor and marched day and night, arriving in one night's travel.
translations.idiomatic: They marched without pitching camp and covered the distance in a single night.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，賊眾又出，列陳於城外。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the enemy masses came out again and drew up battle lines outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Wei army came out again and formed battle lines outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 方平諸軍並成列，安都并領馬軍，方平悉勒步卒，左右掎角之，餘諸義軍並於城西南列陳。

translations.literal: Fangping's armies all completed their lines; Andu together led the cavalry; Fangping fully commanded the foot soldiers, with left and right in pincer; the remaining loyal armies all drew up battle lines southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping's troops finished forming up. Andu took the cavalry while Fangping led all the infantry in a pincer. The other volunteer columns lined up southwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 方平謂安都曰：「今勍敵在前，堅城在後，是吾取死之日。

translations.literal: Fangping said to Andu, "Now a fierce enemy is before us and a strong city behind—this is the day we must seek death.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping said to Andu, "A powerful enemy stands before us and a walled city behind. Today is the day we stake our lives.

sentences.zh: 卿若不進，我當斬卿；

translations.literal: If you do not advance, I shall behead you;
translations.idiomatic: If you do not charge, I will cut off your head.

sentences.zh: 我若不進，卿當斬我也。」

translations.literal: if I do not advance, you should behead me."
translations.idiomatic: If I hang back, you may cut off mine."

sentences.zh: 安都曰：「善，卿言是也。

translations.literal: Andu said, "Good—you speak rightly.
translations.idiomatic: Andu answered, "Well said—you are right.

sentences.zh: 我豈惜身命乎。」

translations.literal: Would I spare my own life?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I value my life?"

sentences.zh: 遂合戰。

translations.literal: They then joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: They closed and fought.

sentences.zh: 時元怙方至，悉偃旗鼓，士馬皆銜枚，潛師伏甲而進，賊未之覺也。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanhu had just arrived; he stilled all drums and banners, men and horses all bore gags in the mouth, and the hidden army with armor laid by advanced—the enemy did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhu had just arrived. He silenced drums and banners, gagged every man and horse, and advanced with hidden armor while the enemy still knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 方平等方與虜交鋒，而元怙勒眾從城南門函道直出，北向結陳，旌旗甚盛，鼓譟而前，出賊不意，虜眾大駭。

translations.literal: Fangping and the others were just crossing blades with the barbarians when Yuanhu led the masses straight out through the covered way of the south gate, formed battle lines facing north with banners very grand, and drummed and clamored forward—catching the enemy unawares, and the barbarian masses were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping's men were already locked with the Wei when Yuanhu burst through the covered way of the south gate, formed line facing north under a blaze of banners, and charged with a thunder of drums. The enemy had not expected him and panicked.

sentences.zh: 元怙與幢主宗越，率手下猛騎，以衝賊陳，一軍皆馳之。

translations.literal: Yuanhu and standard-bearer Zong Yue led their fierce cavalry to charge the enemy formation, and the whole army galloped after them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhu and standard-bearer Zong Yue led their picked horsemen straight into the Wei line, and the whole column swept after them.

sentences.zh: 安都、方平等督諸軍一時齊奮，士卒無不用命。

translations.literal: Andu, Fangping, and the others directed the armies to strive forward all at once; no soldier failed to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Andu and Fangping drove every unit forward at once, and not a man held back.

sentences.zh: 安都不堪其憤，橫矛直前，出入賊陳，殺傷者甚多，流血凝肘，矛折，易之復入。

translations.literal: Andu could not bear his fury; spear levelled he went straight forward, entering and leaving the enemy formation; the killed and wounded were very many; blood congealed on his elbows; his spear broke, he replaced it and entered again.
translations.idiomatic: Andu, unable to contain his rage, levelled his spear and drove straight through the enemy ranks again and again. Blood caked his elbows. His spear snapped; he took another and went back in.

sentences.zh: 軍副譚金率騎從而奔之。

translations.literal: Army deputy Tan Jin led cavalry galloping after him.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Tan Jin led the cavalry in his wake.

sentences.zh: 自詰旦而戰，至于日昃，虜眾大潰，斬張是連提，又斬三千餘級，投河赴塹死者甚眾，面縛軍門者二千餘人。

translations.literal: From dawn they fought until the sun declined; the barbarian masses were greatly routed; Zhang Shilian was beheaded, and more than three thousand heads were also cut; very many who threw themselves into the river or leaped into ditches died; more than two thousand were bound facing inward at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: The battle ran from dawn until midafternoon. The Wei army collapsed. Zhang Shilian was killed and more than three thousand heads were taken. Countless men drowned in the river or fell into the ditches. More than two thousand captives were bound before the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 元景輕騎晨至，虜兵之面縛者多河內人，元景詰之曰：「汝等怨王澤不浹，請命無所，今並為虜盡力，便是本無善心。

translations.literal: Yuanjing came at dawn with light cavalry; many of the bound-facing enemy soldiers were men of Henei. Yuanjing questioned them, saying, "You resent that royal grace does not reach you and have nowhere to plead your case; now you all exert yourselves fully for the barbarians—this shows you originally had no good heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing arrived at dawn with a light escort. Many of the bound prisoners were from Henei. He questioned them: "You complain that the court's grace never reached you and that you had nowhere to turn. Yet now you fought your hardest for the Wei. That shows where your hearts truly lay.

sentences.zh: 順附者存拯，從惡者誅滅，欲知王師正如此爾。」

translations.literal: Those who submit in accord are preserved and rescued; those who follow evil are punished and destroyed—know that the royal army is just like this."
translations.idiomatic: Those who yield will be spared; those who cling to the enemy will be destroyed. That is how the imperial army deals with you."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「虐虜見驅，後出赤族，以騎蹙步，未戰先死，此親將軍所見，非敢背中國也。」

translations.literal: They all said, "The cruel barbarians drove us; those who lagged behind had their whole clans exterminated; cavalry pressed the foot soldiers—before battle we were already as good as dead. This the general himself has seen; we did not dare turn our backs on China."
translations.idiomatic: They answered together, "The Wei drove us at spear-point. Anyone who fell behind lost his whole clan. Their cavalry herded our foot soldiers—we were dead men before the fight began. Your Lordship saw it yourself. We did not willingly turn against the empire."

sentences.zh: 諸將欲盡殺之，元景以為不可，曰：「今王旗北掃，當令仁聲先路。」

translations.literal: The generals wished to kill them all; Yuanjing thought it could not be done and said, "Now the royal banners sweep north; we should let benevolent renown go before."
translations.idiomatic: The other commanders wanted to kill them all, but Yuanjing refused. "The imperial banners are sweeping north," he said. "Let mercy go before the army."

sentences.zh: 乃悉釋而遣之，家在關裏者，符守關諸軍聽出，皆稱萬歲而去。

translations.literal: He then released and sent them all away; those whose families were inside the passes were given writs for the garrison troops holding the passes to allow them out, and all cried "Long live!" as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: He released every man. Those with families inside the passes were given passes allowing them through the border garrisons. They shouted their thanks and went home.

sentences.zh: 誕以崤、陝既定，其地宜撫，以弘農劉寬虯行東弘農太守。

translations.literal: Dan, because Xiao and Shaan were already settled and the region should be pacified, made Liu Kuangqiu of Hongnong acting Administrator of East Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiao Mountain and Shaan secured, Dan judged the region needed a civil hand and appointed Liu Kuangqiu of Hongnong acting administrator of East Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 給元景鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was given one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was granted a full band of martial music.

sentences.zh: 法起率眾次于潼關。

translations.literal: Faqi led the masses and halted at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi marched his force to Tong Pass and encamped there.

sentences.zh: 先是，建義將軍華山太守劉槐糾合義兵攻關城，拔之，力少不固。

translations.literal: Earlier, Establishing Righteousness General and Administrator of Huashan Liu Huai had gathered loyal troops to attack the pass city, took it, but with too few forces could not hold it firm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, establishing righteousness general and Huashan administrator Liu Huai had rallied volunteers, stormed the pass city, and taken it—but his force was too small to hold it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又集眾以應王師，法起次潼關，槐亦至。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he again gathered the masses to respond to the royal army; Faqi halted at Tong Pass and Huai also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he gathered his men again to join the imperial advance. When Faqi reached Tong Pass, Huai came up as well.

sentences.zh: 賊關城戍主婁須望旗奔潰，虜眾溺於河者甚眾。

translations.literal: The enemy pass-city garrison commander Lou Xu saw the banners and fled in rout; very many of the barbarian masses drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei garrison commander Lou Xu saw their banners and broke. Many of his men drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 法起與槐即據潼關。

translations.literal: Faqi and Huai at once seized Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi and Huai immediately occupied Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 虜蒲城鎮主遣偽帥何難於封陵堆列三營以擬法起。

translations.literal: The enemy Pucheng garrison commander sent the false commander He Nan to array three camps at Fengling Mound to oppose Faqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commander at Pucheng sent the officer He Nan to pitch three camps at Fengling Mound to block Faqi.

sentences.zh: 法起長驅入關，行王、檀故壘。

translations.literal: Faqi drove deep into the pass, marching past the old encampments of Wang and Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi pressed deep into the pass, marching past the old camps of Wang and Tan.

sentences.zh: 虜謂直向長安，何難率眾欲濟河以截軍後，法起回軍臨河，縱兵射之，賊退散。

translations.literal: The barbarians thought he was heading straight for Chang'an; He Nan led the masses intending to cross the river to cut the army's rear; Faqi turned the army to face the river, loosed troops to shoot at them, and the enemy dispersed in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei thought he was marching straight on Chang'an. He Nan tried to cross the river and cut off his rear. Faqi wheeled to the riverbank, poured arrows into them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 關中諸義徒並處處鋒起，四山羌、胡咸皆請奮。

translations.literal: Loyal volunteers throughout Guanzhong rose on every side; Qiang and Hu on the four mountains all asked to fight fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalists rose throughout Guanzhong, and Qiang and Hu from the surrounding hills all volunteered to fight.

sentences.zh: 誕又遣揚武將軍康元撫領二千人出上洛，受元景節度，援方平於函谷。

translations.literal: Dan again sent Raising Martial General Kang Yuanfu leading two thousand men out from Shangluo, subject to Yuanjing's command, to reinforce Fangping at Hangu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan also sent raising martial general Kang Yuanfu with two thousand men from Shangluo under Yuanjing's orders to reinforce Fangping at Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 元景去，賊眾向關。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing departed, the enemy masses moved toward the pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanjing left, the Wei army turned toward the pass.

sentences.zh: 時軍中食盡，元景回據白楊嶺，賊定未至，更下山進弘農，入湖關口，虜蒲阪戍主泰州刺史杜道生率眾二萬至閿鄉水，去湖關一百二十里。

translations.literal: At that time provisions in the army were exhausted; Yuanjing withdrew to hold Baiyang Ridge. The rebels had not yet arrived; he again descended the mountain and advanced on Hongnong, entering Huguan Pass. Du Daosheng, the barbarian garrison commander at Puban and Inspector of Taizhou, led twenty thousand men to the Wenxiang River, one hundred and twenty li from Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: The army had run out of food, so Yuanjing pulled back to defend Baiyang Ridge. Before the enemy could arrive, he marched down again toward Hongnong and entered Huguan Pass. Meanwhile Du Daosheng—the Northern Wei garrison chief at Puban and governor of Taizhou—brought twenty thousand troops to the Wenxiang River, only a hundred and twenty li from Huguan.

sentences.zh: 元景募精勇一千人，夜斫賊營，迷失道，天曉而反。

translations.literal: Yuanjing recruited a thousand elite warriors and at night raided the rebel camp; they lost their way and returned at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing raised a thousand picked men for a night attack on the enemy camp, but they lost their way in the dark and came back at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 道生率手下驍銳縱兵射之，鋒刃既交，虜又奔散。

translations.literal: Daosheng led his handpicked fierce troops to unleash arrows upon them; once blades crossed, the barbarians again scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng led his best fighters in a volley of arrows, but as soon as blades met, the Wei troops broke and fled once more.

sentences.zh: 時北討諸軍王玄謨等敗退，虜遂深入。

translations.literal: At that time the northern expedition armies under Wang Xuamo and others were defeated and withdrew, and the barbarians then pressed deep inward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuamo and the other northern expedition forces had already been beaten back, allowing the Wei army to drive deep into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 太祖以元景不宜獨進，且令班師。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen considered that Yuanjing should not advance alone and additionally ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen decided Yuanjing should not press forward on his own and ordered a general retreat.

sentences.zh: 元景乃率諸將自湖關度白楊嶺，出于長洲，安都斷後，宗越副之。

translations.literal: Yuanjing then led the generals from Huguan over Baiyang Ridge, emerging at Changzhou; An Du covered the rear, with Zong Yue as his second.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing led his officers out through Huguan, over Baiyang Ridge, and down to Changzhou, with An Du in the rearguard and Zong Yue supporting him.

sentences.zh: 法起自潼關向商城，與元景會，季明亦從胡谷南歸，並有功而入，士馬旌旗甚盛。

translations.literal: Fa Qi came from Tong Pass toward Shangcheng and joined Yuanjing; Jiming also returned south through Hogu. All entered having achieved merit, with troops, horses, and banners very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Qi marched from Tong Pass toward Shangcheng to meet Yuanjing, while Jiming came south through Hogu Pass. Each column returned with creditable victories, and their soldiers, horses, and banners made a splendid show.

sentences.zh: 誕登城望之，以鞍下馬迎元景。

translations.literal: Dan mounted the wall to watch them; he dismounted from the saddle and went to welcome Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan climbed the city wall to watch the approach, then dismounted and went out on foot to greet Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 除寧朔將軍、京兆廣平二郡太守，於樊城立府舍，率所領居之，統行北蠻事。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Jingzhao and Guangping; he established official quarters at Fancheng, led his command to dwell there, and oversaw northern barbarian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was made General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Jingzhao and Guangping, set up his headquarters at Fancheng with his troops, and was put in charge of affairs with the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 龐季明為定蠻長，薛安都為後軍行參軍，魯方平為寧蠻參軍。

translations.literal: Pang Jiming was made Chief Who Settles the Barbarians; Xue An Du was made Rear Army Acting Commandant; Lu Fangping was made Barbarian-Pacifying Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jiming became Chief Who Settles the Barbarians, Xue An Du Rear Army Acting Commandant, and Lu Fangping Barbarian-Pacifying Commandant.

sentences.zh: 臧質為雍州，除元景為冠軍司馬、襄陽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi was made Governor of Yong Province; Yuanjing was appointed Champion Major and Grand Administrator of Xiangyang, retaining his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi took over Yong Province, Yuanjing was named Champion Major and governor of Xiangyang while keeping his existing rank as general.

sentences.zh: 魯爽向虎牢，復使元景率安都等北出至關城，關城棄戍走，即據之。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang advanced toward Hulao; he again had Yuanjing lead An Du and others north to Guancheng; the garrison abandoned the post and fled, and they immediately seized it.
translations.idiomatic: As Lu Shuang moved on Hulao, Yuanjing was sent north again with An Du and others to Guancheng; the garrison fled without a fight, and he occupied the town at once.

sentences.zh: 元景至洪關，欲進與安都濟河攻杜道生於蒲阪，會爽退，復還。

translations.literal: Yuanjing reached Hong Pass and wished to advance with An Du to cross the river and attack Du Daosheng at Puban; when Shuang withdrew, he returned again.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Pass Yuanjing planned to cross the river with An Du and strike Du Daosheng at Puban, but Lu Shuang's retreat forced him to pull back.

sentences.zh: 再出北討，威信著於境外。

translations.literal: Going out again on northern expedition, his prestige and authority were established beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On his second northern campaign his reputation for power and integrity spread beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又使率所領進西陽，會伐五水蠻。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to lead his command to advance on Xiyang and join in attacking the Wushui barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was next sent with his troops to Xiyang to take part in the campaign against the Wushui barbarians.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討元凶，以為諮議參軍，領中兵，加冠軍將軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to punish the prime villain, Yuanjing was made Advisory Adjutant, commanding the central troops, promoted to Champion General, with his grand administrator title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched east to destroy the usurper Liu Shao, Yuanjing was appointed Advisory Adjutant in charge of the central army, promoted to Champion General, and kept his governorship.

sentences.zh: 配萬人為前鋒，宗慤、薛安都等十三軍皆隸焉。

translations.literal: Ten thousand men were assigned to him as vanguard; the thirteen armies of Zong Que, Xue An Du, and others were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was given ten thousand men as the vanguard, with thirteen armies under Zong Que, Xue An Du, and others subordinated to him.

sentences.zh: 元景與朝士書曰：「國禍寃深，凶人肆逆，民神崩憤，若無天地。

translations.literal: Yuanjing wrote to court officials, saying: "The nation's calamity is deep and grievance profound; the vicious man indulges in rebellion; people and spirits collapse in outrage as if heaven and earth were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing wrote to fellow officials: "The realm suffers a grievous national disaster; a wicked man has risen in open rebellion, and gods and men alike are convulsed with rage, as though heaven and earth had ceased to exist.

sentences.zh: 南中郎親率義師，剪討元惡，司徒、臧冠軍並同大舉，舳艫千里，購賞之利備之。

translations.literal: The Southern Central Commander personally leads the righteous army to cut down and punish the prime evil; the Minister over the Masses and Champion Zang both launch great efforts together; boats stretch for a thousand li; the rewards of bounty are fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Central Commander is personally leading a righteous army to destroy the chief villain; the Minister over the Masses and Champion Zang are both mobilizing on the same scale, with war fleets stretching for a thousand li and generous bounties already posted.

sentences.zh: 元景不武，忝任行間，總勒精勇，先鋒道路，勢乘上流，眾兼百倍。

translations.literal: Yuanjing is not martial; I shamefully hold a post in the ranks, mustering elite courage, clearing the vanguard's path; the momentum rides the upper stream, and our forces are a hundredfold combined.
translations.idiomatic: I am no warrior, yet I am honored to serve in the field, gathering elite troops to open the vanguard's way; we hold the advantage of the upstream current and our numbers are many times greater.

sentences.zh: 諸賢弈世忠義，身為國良，皆受遇先朝，荷榮日久，而拘逼寇廷，莫由申効，想聞今問，悲慶兼常。

translations.literal: You worthy men have loyalty and righteousness through generations; your persons are pillars of the state; all received favor from the former court and have borne glory for long days—yet confined and forced within the rebel court, you have no means to render effect; thinking of hearing today's news, grief and joy are both beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: You have served the dynasty with hereditary loyalty and are true pillars of the state, long favored by the previous emperor—yet trapped under the usurper's court you could do nothing until now. Learning of our cause, you must feel joy and sorrow in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 大行屆道，廓清惟始，企遲面對，展雪哀情。」

translations.literal: The great journey approaches the Way; sweeping clarity has only just begun; I long to face you in person and unfold and wash away grieving sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: The great undertaking is at hand and order will soon be restored; I eagerly await meeting you face to face to share our grief and joy."

sentences.zh: 時義軍船率小陋，慮水戰不敵，至蕪湖，元景大喜，倍道兼行，聞石頭出戰艦，乃於江寧步上，於板橋立柵以自固。

translations.literal: At that time the righteous army's boats were generally small and crude; fearing they could not match the enemy in naval combat, upon reaching Wuhu Yuanjing was greatly pleased and advanced at double speed. Hearing that Shitou had sent out warships, he then went ashore on foot at Jiangning and established palisades at Banqiao to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist fleet was mostly small and poorly built, and they worried they could not win on the water. Yuanjing was delighted when they reached Wuhu and pressed forward at forced march. Learning that enemy warships had sortied from Shitou, he went ashore at Jiangning on foot and fortified himself with a stockade at Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 進據陰山，遣薛安都率馬軍至南岸，元景潛至新亭，依山建壘，東西據險。

translations.literal: He advanced to occupy Yinshan, sent Xue An Du to lead cavalry to the south bank; Yuanjing secretly reached Xinting, built ramparts relying on the mountain, and held strategic points east and west.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yinshan, sent Xue An Du with the cavalry to the south bank, and himself stole up to Xinting, where he built fortifications along the hills and secured the passes on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 世祖復遣龍驤將軍、行參軍程天祚率眾赴之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu again sent Dragon Cavalry General and Acting Commandant Cheng Tianzuo to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu also dispatched Dragon Cavalry General and Acting Commandant Cheng Tianzuo with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 天祚又於東南據高丘，屯砦柵。

translations.literal: Tianzuo again occupied a high hill in the southeast and encamped with stockades and palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo took a hill in the southeast as well and put up camp fortifications there.

sentences.zh: 凡歸順來奔者，皆勸元景速進，元景曰：「不然。

translations.literal: All who came over in submission and fled to join urged Yuanjing to advance quickly; Yuanjing said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Every defector who came over urged Yuanjing to attack at once. Yuanjing replied, "No.

sentences.zh: 理順難恃，同惡相濟，輕進無防，實啟寇心。

translations.literal: Right principle is hard to rely on; those who share evil assist one another; rash advance without defense truly opens the enemy's heart to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness alone is no guarantee; evildoers will rally to one another. A careless advance without defenses will only embolden the enemy.

sentences.zh: 當倚我之不可勝，豈幸寇之不攻哉。」

translations.literal: One should rely on our being unconquerable—how could one count on the enemy's not attacking?"
translations.idiomatic: We should rely on making ourselves unbeatable, not on hoping the enemy chooses not to attack.

sentences.zh: 元景營壘未立，為龍驤將軍詹叔兒覘知之，勸劭出戰，不許。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's camp and ramparts were not yet established; Dragon Cavalry General Zhan Shu'er reconnoitered and learned this, urging Shao to go out to battle, but he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yuanjing's defenses were finished, Dragon Cavalry General Zhan Shu'er spotted the weakness and urged Liu Shao to strike, but Shao refused.

sentences.zh: 經日，乃水陸出軍，劭自登朱雀門督戰。

translations.literal: After a day passed, Shao then sent out troops by land and water; Shao himself mounted Zhuque Gate to oversee the battle.
translations.idiomatic: A day later Liu Shao finally sent forces by land and sea, personally directing the battle from Zhuque Gate.

sentences.zh: 軍至瓦官寺，與義軍游邏相逢，游邏退走，賊遂薄壘。

translations.literal: The army reached Waguan Temple, met the righteous army's patrol, the patrol retreated and fled, and the rebels then pressed close to the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's troops reached Waguan Temple, clashed with loyalist scouts who fell back, and the rebel force closed in on Yuanjing's camp.

sentences.zh: 劭以元景壘塹未立，可得平地决戰，既至，柴柵已堅，倉卒無攻具，便使肉薄攻之。

translations.literal: Shao thought Yuanjing's ramparts and moats were not yet established and that he could decide the battle on open ground; when he arrived, the wooden palisades were already strong, and in haste there were no siege tools, so he had them attack at close quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao had expected to find Yuanjing's trenches unfinished and fight on open ground, but by the time he arrived the palisades were solid. With no siege equipment ready, he ordered a frontal assault.

sentences.zh: 元景宿令軍中曰：「鼓繁氣易衰，叫數力易竭。

translations.literal: Yuanjing had long before ordered the army: "When drums are frequent, spirit easily fades; when shouting is repeated, strength easily exhausts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing had already told his men, "Heavy drumming wears down morale, and constant shouting drains your strength.

sentences.zh: 但各銜枚疾戰，一聽吾營鼓音。」

translations.literal: Each should only hold a gag in the mouth and fight swiftly; listen only to the drum sound from my camp."
translations.idiomatic: Bite your gag and fight hard, and wait for my signal drum alone.

sentences.zh: 賊步將魯秀、王羅漢、劉簡之、騎將常伯與等及其士卒，皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: The rebel infantry generals Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, Liu Jianzhi, cavalry generals Chang Boyu and others, and their soldiers all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel infantry commanders Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, and Liu Jianzhi, the cavalry commander Chang Boyu, and their troops all fought with desperate fury.

sentences.zh: 劉簡之先攻西南，頻得燒草舫，略渡人。

translations.literal: Liu Jianzhi first attacked the southwest, repeatedly obtaining burned grass boats, and somewhat crossed men over.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianzhi hit the southwest first, using burning straw rafts to ferry some of his men across.

sentences.zh: 程天祚柴未立，亦為所摧。

translations.literal: Cheng Tianzuo's palisades were not yet established, and he too was broken by them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tianzuo's fortifications were not yet complete, and he too was overrun.

sentences.zh: 王羅漢等攻壘北門，賊艦亦至。

translations.literal: Wang Luohan and others attacked the north gate of the ramparts, and rebel warships also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luohan and his men assaulted the north gate while enemy ships closed in from the river.

sentences.zh: 元景水陸受敵，意氣彌強，麾下勇士悉遣出戰，左右唯留數人宣傳。

translations.literal: Yuanjing was attacked by land and water; his fighting spirit grew stronger; all the brave warriors under his command he sent out to battle; by his sides he kept only a few men for relaying orders.
translations.idiomatic: Beset on land and water, Yuanjing only fought harder, sending every able fighter into the fray and keeping just a few aides at his side to carry orders.

sentences.zh: 分軍助程天祚，天祚還得固柴，因此破賊。

translations.literal: He divided forces to assist Cheng Tianzuo; Tianzuo was again able to secure his palisades, and thereby defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He detached troops to reinforce Cheng Tianzuo, who was able to hold his line and turn the tide against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 元景察賊衰竭，乃命開壘，鼓譟以奔之，賊眾大潰，透淮死者甚多。

translations.literal: Yuanjing observed the rebels' exhaustion and then ordered the ramparts opened, with drum clamor to charge them; the rebel masses greatly collapsed, and many died crossing through the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the enemy spent, Yuanjing ordered the gates opened and sent his men charging with a thunder of drums. The rebel army broke completely, and many drowned or were killed trying to cross the canal.

sentences.zh: 劭更率餘眾自來攻壘，復大破之，其所殺傷，過於前戰。

translations.literal: Shao again led the remaining masses himself to attack the ramparts and was again greatly defeated; the killed and wounded exceeded the previous battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao personally led another assault with his remaining troops and was crushed again, with even heavier casualties than the first fight.

sentences.zh: 劭手斬退者不能禁，奔還宮，僅以身免，蕭斌被創。

translations.literal: Shao personally beheaded those who retreated and could not restrain them; they fled back to the palace; he barely escaped with his body intact; Xiao Bin was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao himself cut down retreating soldiers but could not stop the rout. He raced back to the palace and barely escaped with his life, while Xiao Bin was wounded.

sentences.zh: 簡之收兵而止，陳猶未散。

translations.literal: Jianzhi gathered troops and stopped; the battle formation had not yet dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianzhi regrouped his men and held his ground; his formation had not yet broken up.

sentences.zh: 元景復出薄之，乃走，競投死馬澗，澗為之滿，斬簡之及軍主姚叔藝、王江寶、朱明智、諸葛邈之等，水軍主褚湛之、副劉道存並來歸順。

translations.literal: Yuanjing again went out and pressed close to them; they then fled, competing to throw themselves into Dead Horse Stream; the stream was filled by it; he beheaded Jianzhi and army commanders Yao Shuyi, Wang Jiangbao, Zhu Mingzhi, Zhuge Miaozhi, and others; naval commander Chu Zhenzhi and deputy Liu Daocun both came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing sallied forth again and drove them off. They stampeded into Dead Horse Gully until the stream was choked with bodies. Liu Jianzhi and commanders Yao Shuyi, Wang Jiangbao, Zhu Mingzhi, and Zhuge Miaozhi were killed, while naval officers Chu Zhenzhi and Liu Daocun defected to the loyalists.

sentences.zh: 上至新亭即位，以元景為侍中，領左衞將軍，轉使持節、監雍梁南北秦四州荊州之竟陵隨二郡諸軍事、前將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended at Xinting, he made Yuanjing Palace Attendant, commanding Left Guard General, transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of military affairs of the four provinces Yong, Liang, South Qin, and North Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui of Jing Province, Forward General, Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu took the throne at Xinting, he made Yuanjing Palace Attendant and Left Guard General, then Inspector of Yong Province and Forward General with authority over Yong, Liang, northern and southern Qin, and parts of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上在巴口，問元景：「事平，何所欲？」

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Bakou, he asked Yuanjing: "When affairs are settled, what do you desire?"
translations.idiomatic: At Bakou the new emperor asked Yuanjing, "When this is over, what reward do you want?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若有過恩，願還鄉里。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If there is excessive grace, I wish to return to my homeland."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing answered, "If Your Majesty grants me too much favor, I would only ask to go home.

sentences.zh: 故有此授。

translations.literal: Therefore he received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: That was why he received the Yongzhou post instead of a capital appointment.

sentences.zh: 初，臧質起義，以南譙王義宣闇弱易制，欲相推奉，潛報元景，使率所領西還。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zang Zhi raised righteous arms, considering that Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan was dim-witted, weak, and easy to control, he wished to promote and enthrone him; he secretly informed Yuanjing to lead his command west in return.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the uprising Zang Zhi, believing Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao weak and easy to manipulate, planned to put him on the throne and secretly asked Yuanjing to march west with his troops.

sentences.zh: 元景即以質書呈世祖，語其使曰：「臧冠軍當是未知殿下義舉爾。

translations.literal: Yuanjing immediately presented Zhi's letter to Emperor Xiaowu and told his messenger: "Champion Zang presumably does not yet know of Your Highness's righteous undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing handed Zang Zhi's letter straight to Emperor Xiaowu and told the messenger, "Champion Zang must not know yet that Your Highness has risen in righteous arms.

sentences.zh: 方應伐逆，不容西還。」

translations.literal: We are just now supposed to punish rebellion; we cannot allow a westward return."
translations.idiomatic: We are here to punish the usurper; a westward march is out of the question.

sentences.zh: 質以此恨之。

translations.literal: Zhi therefore resented him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi never forgave him for it.

sentences.zh: 及元景為雍州刺史，質慮其為荊、江後患，建議爪牙不宜遠出。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing became Inspector of Yong Province, Zhi feared he would become a later trouble for Jing and Jiang provinces and proposed that claw-and-fang henchmen should not be sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanjing became governor of Yongzhou, Zang Zhi worried he would become a threat to the Jiang and Jing regions and argued that the emperor's strongarm should not be posted so far away.

sentences.zh: 上重違其言，更以元景為護軍將軍，領石頭戍事，不拜。

translations.literal: The Emperor heavily went against his words and instead made Yuanjing Protector General, commanding the Shitou garrison affairs; Yuanjing did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated to overrule him and offered Yuanjing the post of Protector General in charge of Shitou—but Yuanjing declined.

sentences.zh: 徙領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，曲江縣公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commanding General, additionally made Regular Palace Attendant, Duke of Qujiang County, with a fisc of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was instead made Commanding General and Regular Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang with three thousand taxable households.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年正月，魯爽反，遣左衞將軍王玄謨討之，加元景撫軍，假節置佐，係玄謨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xiaojian, Lu Shuang rebelled; the Emperor dispatched Left Guard General Wang Xuamo to punish him, promoted Yuanjing to Pacification General, granted provisional staff and set adjutants, attaching him to Xuamo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xiaojian 454 Lu Shuang rebelled. The court sent Left Guard General Wang Xuamo against him, promoted Yuanjing to Pacification General with provisional staff, and placed him under Xuamo's command.

sentences.zh: 復以為都督雍梁南北秦四州荊州之竟陵隨二郡諸軍事、撫軍將軍、領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was again made Area Commander of military affairs of the four provinces Yong, Liang, South Qin, and North Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui of Jing Province, Pacification General, concurrently Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Inspector of Yong Province, with Bearer of the Staff of Authority as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named area commander and Pacification General over Yong, Liang, Qin north and south, and parts of Jingzhou, still holding the staff of authority as governor of Yong and Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 臧質、義宣並反，玄謨南據梁山，夾江為壘，垣護之、薛安都渡據歷陽，元景出屯采石。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi and Yixuan both rebelled; Xuamo held Liangshan in the south, building ramparts flanking the river; Yuan Huzhi and Xue An Du crossed to hold Liyang; Yuanjing deployed at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi and Yixuan both rose in revolt, Xuamo fortified Liangshan on the south bank, Yuan Huzhi and Xue An Du seized Liyang on the north, and Yuanjing encamped at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 玄謨聞賊盛，遣司馬管法濟求益兵，上使元景進屯姑孰。

translations.literal: Xuamo heard the rebels were strong and sent Major Guan Faji to request additional troops; the Emperor had Yuanjing advance to encamp at Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing how strong the rebels were, Xuamo sent his major Guan Faji to request reinforcements, and the emperor ordered Yuanjing forward to Gudu.

sentences.zh: 元景使將武念前進，質遣將龐法起襲姑孰，值念至，擊破之，法起單船走。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sent General Wu Nian to advance; Zhi sent General Pang Faqi to raid Gudu; when Nian arrived, he defeated them; Faqi fled in a single boat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing sent General Wu Nian ahead; Zang Zhi countered with Pang Faqi to strike Gudu, but Wu Nian routed the attackers and Pang Faqi escaped alone in one boat.

sentences.zh: 質攻陷玄謨西壘，玄謨使垣護之告元景曰：「今餘東岸萬人，賊軍數倍，強弱不敵，謂宜還就節下協力當之。」

translations.literal: Zhi captured and overthrew Xuamo's western ramparts; Xuamo sent Yuan Huzhi to tell Yuanjing: "Now the remaining eastern bank has ten thousand men; the rebel army is several times more; strong and weak do not match; I say we should return to join under your command and coordinate to meet them."
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi overran Xuamo's western fort, and Xuamo sent Yuan Huzhi to tell Yuanjing, "I have only ten thousand men left on the east bank, while the rebels outnumber us several times over. We cannot hold. I think we should fall back to you and fight together under your command.

sentences.zh: 元景謂護之曰：「師有常刑，不可先退。

translations.literal: Yuanjing said to Huzhi: "The army has fixed punishments; one cannot retreat first.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing replied, "Desertion is punished by death. We cannot pull back first.

sentences.zh: 賊眾雖多，猜而不整，今當卷甲赴之。」

translations.literal: Though the rebel masses are many, they are suspicious and not orderly; now we should roll up armor and go to them."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy may be numerous, but they are divided and disorganized. I am going to rush to your aid at once.

sentences.zh: 護之曰：「逆徒皆云南州有三萬人，而麾下裁十分之一，若往造賊，虛實立見，則賊氣成矣。」

translations.literal: Huzhi said: "The rebel traitors all say the Southern Province has thirty thousand men, but under your command there is barely one-tenth; if we go to meet the rebels, empty and full will immediately be seen, and rebel morale will be formed."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi argued, "The rebels believe we have thirty thousand men from the south. If you come with only a fraction of that, they will see how weak we really are and their spirits will soar.

sentences.zh: 元景納其言，悉遣精兵助玄謨，以羸弱居守。

translations.literal: Yuanjing accepted his words and sent all elite troops to assist Xuamo, keeping the weak to hold the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing took his advice and sent nearly all his best troops to Xuamo, leaving only weak forces to hold Gudu.

sentences.zh: 所遣軍多張旗幟，梁山望之如數萬人，皆曰：「京師兵悉至。」

translations.literal: The troops sent mostly spread banners and flags; viewed from Liangshan they looked like tens of thousands of men; all said: "The capital's troops have all arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Those troops flew countless banners, and from Liangshan they looked like tens of thousands. Everyone cried, "The capital army has arrived in full strength!

sentences.zh: 於是眾心乃安，由是克捷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hearts of the masses were settled, and thereby victory was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Morale steadied, and victory followed.

sentences.zh: 上遣丹陽尹顏竣宣旨慰勞，與沈慶之俱以本號開府儀同三司，封晉安郡公，邑如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Metropolitan Governor of Danyang Yan Jun to proclaim the imperial will to comfort and reward; together with Shen Qingzhi, Yuanjing was granted Opening of the Office with the same precedence as the Three Excellencies under his original title, enfeoffed as Duke of Jin'an Commandery, fisc as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Danyang governor Yan Jun with imperial commendations. Yuanjing and Shen Qingzhi were both granted Grand Prefect honors under their existing titles and Yuanjing was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin'an with his fief unchanged.

sentences.zh: 固讓開府儀同，復為領軍、太子詹事，加侍中。

translations.literal: He firmly declined Opening of the Office with equal precedence; he was again made Commanding General and Household Head of the Heir Apparent, additionally Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the Grand Prefect honor and was instead reappointed Commanding General, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋轉驃騎將軍、本州大中正，領軍、侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Rapid Cavalry General and Chief Rectifier of his home province; Commanding General and Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Rapid Cavalry General and chief rectifier of his native province while retaining Commanding General and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，復加開府儀同三司，又固讓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies was again added; he again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 458 he was again offered Grand Prefect status and again refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷尚書令，太子詹事、侍中、中正如故。

translations.literal: The next year, he was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing; Household Head of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant, and Chief Rectifier as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Director of the Masters of Writing while keeping his posts as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, Palace Attendant, and chief rectifier.

sentences.zh: 以封在嶺南，秋輸艱遠，改封巴東郡公。

translations.literal: Because the enfeoffment was in Lingnan, autumn tribute was arduous and distant; he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because his original fief lay far south in Lingnan and made tax delivery impractical, his title was changed to Duke of Badong.

sentences.zh: 五年，又命左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，侍中、令、中正如故，又讓開府，乃與沈慶之俱依晉密陵侯鄭袤不受司空故事，事在慶之傳。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was again appointed Senior Grandee of the Left and Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies; Palace Attendant, Director, and Chief Rectifier as before; he again declined Opening of the Office; then together with Shen Qingzhi he followed the Jin precedent of Marquis Mi of Zheng Mao's refusing the Minister of Works—matters recorded in Qingzhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was again named Senior Grandee of the Left with Grand Prefect honors while keeping his court posts, declined the Grand Prefect rank again, and followed the Jin precedent of Zheng Mao refusing the Ministry of Works—an episode recounted in Shen Qingzhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 六年，進司空，侍中、令、中正如故，又固讓，乃授侍中、驃騎將軍、南兗州刺史，留衞京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to Minister of Works; Palace Attendant, Director, and Chief Rectifier as before; he again firmly declined; then he was granted Palace Attendant, Rapid Cavalry General, and Inspector of South Yan Province, remaining to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Minister of Works but declined once more and was given Palace Attendant, Rapid Cavalry General, and governor of South Yanzhou while staying in the capital as imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 世祖晏駕，與太宰江夏王義恭、尚書僕射顏師伯並受遺詔輔幼主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu passed away, together with Grand Tutor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo, he jointly received the dying edict to assist the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Yuanjing joined Grand Tutor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and Vice Director Yan Shibo as regents under the late emperor's will.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，領丹陽尹，侍中、將軍如故，給班劍二十人，固辭班劍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently Metropolitan Governor of Danyang; Palace Attendant and General as before; twenty ceremonial swords were granted; he firmly declined the ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Masters of Writing and governor of Danyang, kept his rank as Palace Attendant and general, was offered twenty ceremonial guard swords, and declined the swords.

sentences.zh: 元景起自將帥，及當朝理務，雖非所長，而有弘雅之美。

translations.literal: Yuanjing rose from the rank of general; when handling court governance affairs, though it was not his strength, he had the beauty of broad refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing had risen from the ranks of field commanders; civil administration was not his forte, yet he carried himself with generous elegance.

sentences.zh: 時在朝勳要，多事產業，唯元景獨無所營。

translations.literal: At that time the meritorious and powerful at court mostly pursued estates and business; only Yuanjing alone had nothing he cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Most powerful men at court were busy building estates, but Yuanjing alone invested in nothing.

sentences.zh: 南岸有數十畝菜園，守園人賣得錢二萬送還宅，元景曰：「我立此園種菜，以供家中啖爾。

translations.literal: On the south bank there were several tens of mu of vegetable garden; the garden keeper sold produce and obtained twenty thousand cash, which he sent back to the residence; Yuanjing said: "I established this garden to plant vegetables to supply the household's eating—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a vegetable plot of a few dozen mu on the south bank. When the gardener sold produce for twenty thousand cash and brought the money home, Yuanjing said, "I planted this garden so my family could eat from it.

sentences.zh: 乃復賣菜以取錢，奪百姓之利邪。」

translations.literal: Yet again sell vegetables to obtain money—would that seize the people's profit?"
translations.idiomatic: Am I supposed to sell vegetables for cash and steal a living from common folk?

sentences.zh: 以錢乞守園人。

translations.literal: He gave the money to the garden keeper as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the money back to the gardener.

sentences.zh: 世祖嚴暴異常，元景雖荷寵遇，恒慮及禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was unusually severe and violent; though Yuanjing bore favored treatment, he constantly feared reaching disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was famously brutal, and even amid imperial favor Yuanjing lived in constant fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭及諸大臣，莫不重足屏氣，未嘗敢私往來。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and the various great ministers—none did not stand on tiptoe and hold their breath; none ever dared private coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and the other ministers walked on eggshells and never dared visit one another privately.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，義恭、元景等並相謂曰：「今日始免橫死。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Yigong, Yuanjing, and the others all said to one another: "Today we begin to escape violent death."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Yigong, Yuanjing, and the others told each other, "At last we are spared an arbitrary execution.

sentences.zh: 義恭與義陽等諸王，元景與顏師伯等，常相馳逐，聲樂酣酒，以夜繼晝。

translations.literal: Yigong with the various princes such as Yiyang, and Yuanjing with Yan Shibo and others, constantly raced about together in music and deep drinking, night succeeding day.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong and the princes, Yuanjing and Yan Shibo and their circle, took to feasting and racing about day and night in endless revelry.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝少有凶德，內不能平，殺戴法興後，悖情轉露，義恭、元景等憂懼無計，乃與師伯等謀廢帝立義恭，日夜聚謀，而持疑不能速決。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor in youth had vicious virtue; inwardly he could not be pacified; after killing Dai Faxing, perverse feelings increasingly showed; Yigong, Yuanjing, and the others, anxious and fearful without plan, then with Shibo and others plotted to depose the emperor and establish Yigong; day and night they gathered in counsel, yet held doubts and could not swiftly decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor had been vicious from youth, and after he killed Dai Faxing his depravity broke into the open. Yigong, Yuanjing, and the others, desperate and afraid, joined Yan Shibo in plotting to depose him and put Yigong on the throne. They met night after night but could not bring themselves to act.

sentences.zh: 永光年夏，元景遷使持節、督南豫之宣城諸軍事、即本號開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史，侍中、令如故。

translations.literal: In the summer of the Yongguang era, Yuanjing was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of military affairs of Xuancheng and other regions of South Yu, concurrently his original title Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of South Yu Province; Palace Attendant and Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the Yongguang era Yuanjing was transferred to South Yu as area commander and governor with Grand Prefect honors under his existing title, while keeping Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 未拜，發覺，帝親率宿衞兵自出討之。

translations.literal: Before accepting the appointment, the plot was discovered; the Emperor personally led the palace guard troops himself to go out and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post the plot was discovered, and the emperor himself led the palace guard out to crush it.

sentences.zh: 先稱詔召元景，左右奔告兵刃非常，元景知禍至，整朝服，乘車應召。

translations.literal: First the Emperor proclaimed an edict summoning Yuanjing; attendants ran to tell that weapons were extraordinary; Yuanjing knew disaster had arrived, straightened court robes, mounted a carriage, and responded to the summons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first summoned Yuanjing under imperial pretense. Aides rushed in warning that armed men were abroad. Yuanjing knew his end had come, dressed in full court regalia, and went out in his carriage as ordered.

sentences.zh: 出門逢弟車騎司馬叔仁，戎服率左右壯士數十人欲拒命，元景苦禁之。

translations.literal: Going out the gate he met his younger brother Rapid Cavalry Major Shuren, in military dress leading several tens of strong warriors on his left and right wishing to resist the command; Yuanjing bitterly forbade them.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate he met his brother Shuren, the Rapid Cavalry Major, in armor with several dozen retainers ready to resist. Yuanjing forbade them sternly.

sentences.zh: 既出巷，軍士大至，下車受戮，容色恬然，時年六十。

translations.literal: Once out of the lane, soldiers arrived in great numbers; he descended from the carriage to receive execution; his countenance was calm; he was sixty years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he left the lane the soldiers closed in. He stepped down from his carriage to meet the blade, calm to the last. He was sixty years old.

sentences.zh: 長子慶宗，有幹力，而情性不倫，世祖使元景送還襄陽，於道中賜死。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qingzong had ability and strength, but his disposition and nature were not proper; Emperor Xiaowu had Yuanjing send him back to Xiangyang, and on the road he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qingzong was capable but wayward. Emperor Xiaowu had Yuanjing send him back to Xiangyang, and he was ordered to take his own life on the way.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣宗，豫章王子尚車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: His second son Sizong was Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry Retinue to Prince Zishang of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Sizong served as Attendant in the Rapid Cavalry Retinue of Prince Zishang of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗弟紹宗、共宗、孝宗、文宗、仲宗、成宗、季宗，叔仁弟衞軍諮議參軍僧珍等諸弟姪在京邑及襄陽從死者數十人。

translations.literal: Sizong's younger brothers Shaozong, Gongzong, Xiaozong, Wenzong, Zhongzong, Chengzong, and Jizong; Shuren's younger brother Advisory Adjutant of the Guard Army Sengzhen and other brothers and nephews in the capital region and Xiangyang who followed in death numbered several tens of persons.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers Shaozong, Gongzong, Xiaozong, Wenzong, Zhongzong, Chengzong, and Jizong; Shuren's brother Sengzhen, an Advisory Adjutant of the Guard Army; and dozens of other brothers and nephews in the capital and at Xiangyang were put to death with him.

sentences.zh: 元景少子承宗，及嗣宗子纂，並在孕獲全。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's youngest son Chengzong, and Sizong's son Zuan, both being in the womb, were preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing's youngest son Chengzong and Sizong's unborn son Zuan were spared because their mothers were pregnant.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，令曰：「故侍中、尚書令、驃騎大將軍、巴東郡開國公、新除開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史元景，風度弘簡，體局深沈，正義亮時，恭素範物。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, an edict said: "The late Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Founding Duke of Badong Commandery, newly removed Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of South Yu Province Yuanjing—his bearing was broad and simple, his stature and composure deep and restrained, righteous principle illumined the age, respectful simplicity modeled things for others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he issued an edict: "The late Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, Founding Duke of Badong, newly appointed Grand Prefect, and Governor of South Yu Liu Yuanjing bore himself with broad simplicity and deep composure; his integrity lit the age and his modest courtesy set a standard for all.

sentences.zh: 幽明道盡，則首贊孝圖，盛運開曆，則毗燮皇化。
