translations.literal: When the hidden Way and bright Way were exhausted, then he first assisted the filial design; when flourishing fortune opened the calendar, then he aided and harmonized imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty faced its darkest hour he helped restore filial order; when fortune returned he helped sustain the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 方任孚漢輔，業懋殷衡，而蜂豺肆濫，顯加禍毒，寃動勳烈，悲深朝貫。

translations.literal: Just entrusted as a Han minister-advisor, his achievements flourishing like Yin of Shang—yet jackals and wolves ran wild, openly heaping calamity and poison; injustice moved the meritorious, and grief ran deep among court officials.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just been entrusted with high office and his service was flourishing when jackals and wolves ran amok and openly visited ruin upon him; the injustice stirred the empire's heroes, and grief ran deep through the court.

sentences.zh: 朕承七廟之靈，纂臨寶業，情典既申，痛悼彌軫，宜崇賁徽冊，以旌忠懿。

translations.literal: We inherit the spirits of the seven temples and succeed to the precious enterprise; feelings and rites having been expressed, grief and mourning grow ever deeper. He should be honored with splendid registers to commemorate loyalty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We who inherit the spirits of the seven temples and hold the imperial throne have already paid him the rites due his feelings, yet our grief only deepens. Let splendid honors be conferred to mark his loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 可追贈使持節、都督南豫江二州諸軍事、太尉，侍中、刺史、國公如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the two provinces of South Yu and Jiang, Grand Marshal, with Palace Attendant, Inspector, and State Duke as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously appointed Grand Marshal and commander of all forces in South Yu and Jiang, retaining his ranks as Palace Attendant, provincial governor, and State Duke.

sentences.zh: 給班劍三十人，羽葆、鼓吹十部，諡曰忠烈公。」

translations.literal: Grant thirty ceremonial swords, ten sets of feather canopy and military band; posthumous title: Duke of Loyalty and Resoluteness."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him thirty ceremonial swords, ten sets of feathered canopy and military band, and the posthumous title Duke of Loyalty and Resoluteness."

sentences.zh: 叔仁為梁州刺史，黃門郎。

translations.literal: Shuren was Inspector of Liang Province and Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shuren served as Inspector of Liang Province and Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以破臧質功，封宜陽侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating Zang Zhi, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his victory over Zang Zhi he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 元景從兄元怙，大明末，代叔仁為梁州，與晉安王子勛同逆，事敗歸降。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's older clansman Yuan Hu, at the end of the Daming era, replaced Shuren as Inspector of Liang Province, rebelled together with Prince Zixun of Jin'an, and after defeat returned in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hu, an older cousin of Yuanjing, took over Liang Province from Shuren in the late Daming era, joined Prince Zixun of Jin'an in rebellion, and surrendered after their defeat.

sentences.zh: 元景從父弟先宗，大明初，為竟陵王誕司空參軍，誕作亂，殺之，追贈黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's younger paternal cousin Xianzong, in the early Daming era, was a staff officer to Prince Dan of Jingling; when Dan rebelled he was killed, and posthumously awarded Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, a younger cousin of Yuanjing, served on Prince Dan of Jingling's staff in the early Daming era. When Dan rebelled he was executed and later posthumously made Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元景從祖弟光世，先留鄉里，索虜以為折衝將軍、河北太守，封西陵男。

translations.literal: Yuanjing's paternal cousin Guangshi, having remained in the homeland, was by the Northern Wei made General Who Breaks the Charge and Administrator of Hebei, and enfeoffed as Baron of Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi, another cousin of Yuanjing, had stayed behind in their native region. The Northern Wei made him General Who Breaks the Charge and governor of Hebei, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xiling.

sentences.zh: 光世姊夫偽司徒崔浩，虜之相也。

translations.literal: Guangshi's brother-in-law, the Wei Minister of Works Cui Hao, was the barbarians' chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi's brother-in-law was Cui Hao, the Wei Minister of Works and chief minister of the barbarian court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，虜主拓跋燾南寇汝、潁，浩密有異圖，光世要河北義士為浩應。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, the barbarian ruler Tuoba Tao raided south into Ru and Ying; Hao secretly harbored a different design, and Guangshi summoned righteous men of Hebei to respond on Hao's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 27 the Wei ruler Tuoba Tao invaded south toward Ru and Ying. Hao secretly nursed other plans, and Guangshi rallied loyalists in Hebei to rise in his support.

sentences.zh: 浩謀泄被誅，河東大姓坐連謀夷滅者甚眾，光世南奔得免。

translations.literal: Hao's plot leaked and he was executed; very many great clans of Hedong were exterminated for complicity in the plot, while Guangshi fled south and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao's conspiracy was exposed he was executed, and many great families of Hedong were wiped out for involvement. Guangshi fled south and survived.

sentences.zh: 太祖以為振武將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu appointed him General Who Stirs Martial Ardor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu made him General Who Stirs Martial Ardor.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和中，左將軍，直閤。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor, in the Jinghe era, he was Left General and Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor, during the Jinghe reign, he served as Left General and Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，光世參謀，以為右衞將軍，封開國縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the disorder, Guangshi took part in planning; he was made Right Guard General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Kaiguo County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming put down the rebellion, Guangshi helped plan the campaign and was made Right Guard General and Marquis of Kaiguo County with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 既而四方反叛，同閤宗越、譚金又誅，光世乃北奔薛安都，安都使守下邳城。

translations.literal: Soon afterward rebellions broke out on all sides; Tongge Zongyue and Tan Jin were also executed; Guangshi then fled north to Xue Andu, and Andu had him guard Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions soon erupted everywhere. After Tongge Zongyue and Tan Jin were executed, Guangshi fled north to Xue Andu, who put him in charge of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 及安都招引索虜，光世率眾歸降，太宗宥之，以為順陽太守。

translations.literal: When Andu invited in the Northern Wei, Guangshi led his troops in surrender; Emperor Ming pardoned him and made him Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Andu called in the Northern Wei, Guangshi surrendered with his troops. Emperor Ming spared him and appointed him governor of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 子欣慰謀反，光世賜死。

translations.literal: His son Xinwei plotted rebellion, and Guangshi was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Xinwei plotted rebellion, Guangshi was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯

translations.literal: Yan Shibo
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo

sentences.zh: 顏師伯字長淵，琅邪臨沂人，東揚州刺史竣族兄也。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo, styled Changyuan, was a man of Linyi in Langya and an older clansman of Yan Jun, Inspector of East Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo, styled Changyuan, came from Linyi in Langya and was an older kinsman of Yan Jun, governor of East Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 父邵，剛正有局力，為謝晦所知。

translations.literal: His father Shao was upright and forceful of character and was noticed by Xie Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao was upright and resolute, and won the esteem of Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 晦為領軍，以為司馬，廢立之際，與之參謀。

translations.literal: When Hui became Director-General of the Army, he made Shao his Chief of Staff; at the time of deposing and enthroning emperors, Shao took part in planning with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui became commander of the palace guard, he made Shao his chief of staff, and Shao helped him plan the deposition and enthronement.

sentences.zh: 晦鎮江陵，請為諮議參軍，領錄事，軍府之務悉委焉。

translations.literal: When Hui garrisoned Jiangling, he requested Shao as Advisory Adjutant in charge of records; all affairs of the military headquarters were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui took up his post at Jiangling, he brought Shao in as advisory adjutant and chief recorder, leaving the entire headquarters in his hands.

sentences.zh: 邵慮晦將有禍，求為竟陵太守，未及之郡，值晦見討，晦與邵謀起兵距朝廷，邵飲藥死。

translations.literal: Shao feared that Hui would meet disaster, requested appointment as Administrator of Jingling, and before reaching the commandery, when Hui was attacked, Hui and Shao plotted to raise troops to resist the court; Shao drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disaster for Hui, Shao asked to be made governor of Jingling. Before he could take up the post, Hui was attacked. Hui and Shao plotted to raise troops against the court, and Shao took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 師伯少孤貧，涉獵書傳，頗解聲樂。

translations.literal: Shibo was orphaned and poor in youth, read widely in books and classics, and understood music rather well.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo lost his father early and grew up in poverty. He read widely in the classics and had a fair knowledge of music.

sentences.zh: 劉道產為雍州，以為輔國行參軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Daochan was Inspector of Yong Province, he made Shibo Assistant in the Country-Aiding Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Daochan governed Yong Province, he appointed Shibo assistant in the country-aiding command.

sentences.zh: 弟師仲，妻，臧質女也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shizhong's wife was a daughter of Zang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo's younger brother Shizhong was married to a daughter of Zang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質為徐州，辟師伯為主簿。

translations.literal: When Zhi was Inspector of Xu Province, he recruited Shibo as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi governed Xu Province, he recruited Shibo as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王義季代質為徐州，質薦師伯於義季，義季即命為征西行參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Yiji of Hengyang replaced Zhi as Inspector of Xu Province; Zhi recommended Shibo to Yiji, and Yiji immediately appointed him Western Campaigning Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yiji of Hengyang replaced Zang Zhi at Xu Province, Zhi recommended Shibo to him, and Yiji at once made him western campaigning adjutant.

sentences.zh: 興安侯義賓代義季，世祖代義賓，仍為輔國、安北行參軍。

translations.literal: Marquis Yibin of Xing'an replaced Yiji; Emperor Xiaowu replaced Yibin; Shibo remained Assistant in the Country-Aiding and North-Pacifying commands.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Yibin of Xing'an succeeded Yiji, and Emperor Xiaowu succeeded Yibin. Shibo continued as adjutant in the country-aiding and north-pacifying commands.

sentences.zh: 王景文時為諮議參軍，愛其諧敏，進之世祖。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwen was then Advisory Adjutant; he admired Shibo's wit and quickness and recommended him to Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen, then an advisory adjutant, admired Shibo's quick wit and brought him to Emperor Xiaowu's attention.

sentences.zh: 師伯因求杖節，乃以為徐州主簿。

translations.literal: Shibo thereupon requested a ceremonial staff, and so was made Chief Clerk of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo asked for a ceremonial staff and was appointed chief clerk of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 善於附會，大被知遇。

translations.literal: Skilled at ingratiating himself, he was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept at currying favor and won great favor at court.

sentences.zh: 及去鎮，師伯以主簿送故。

translations.literal: When the prince left his post, Shibo as chief clerk escorted him on his departure.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince left his post, Shibo accompanied him as chief clerk on the formal farewell journey.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，啟太祖請為南中郎府主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu garrisoned Xunyang, he petitioned Emperor Wu to appoint Shibo Chief Clerk of the South Central Commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: While garrisoning Xunyang, Emperor Xiaowu asked Emperor Wu to make Shibo chief clerk of the South Central Commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太祖不許，謂典籤曰：「中郎府主簿那得用顏師伯。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu did not consent and said to the record-keeper: "How can the South Central Commander's chief clerk be Yan Shibo?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu refused and told the record-keeper, "How can Yan Shibo serve as chief clerk of the South Central Commander's headquarters?"

sentences.zh: 世祖啟為長流正佐，太祖又曰：「朝廷不能除之，郎可自板，亦不宜署長流。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu petitioned to make him Senior Administrator; Emperor Wu again said: "The court cannot remove him; my son may appoint by tally himself, but he still should not be assigned Senior Administrator."
translations.idiomatic: The prince then asked for Shibo to be made senior administrator. Emperor Wu replied, "The court cannot dismiss him, but you may appoint him by tally on your own—still, he should not hold the senior administrator's post."

sentences.zh: 世祖乃板為參軍事，署刑獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu then appointed him by tally as Staff Officer and assigned him criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu then appointed Shibo by tally as staff officer and put him in charge of criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 及入討元凶，轉主簿。

translations.literal: When he entered to attack the Primary Culprit, Shibo was transferred to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince marched to punish the Primary Culprit, Shibo was made chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，以為黃門侍郎，隨王誕驃騎長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he made Shibo Yellow Gate Attendant, Chief of Staff to Prince Dan's Rapid Cavalry retinue, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he made Shibo Yellow Gate Attendant, chief of staff to Prince Dan's rapid cavalry retinue, and governor of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 改為驃騎大將軍長史、南濮陽太守，御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Chief of Staff to the Grand General of Rapid Cavalry and Administrator of Nanpuyang, and Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as chief of staff to the Grand General of Rapid Cavalry and governor of Nanpuyang, and also made imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 臧質反，出為寧遠將軍、東陽太守，領兵置佐，以備東道。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi rebelled, Shibo was sent out as General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of Dongyang, leading troops with aides to guard the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi rebelled, Shibo was sent out as General of Distant Pacification and governor of Dongyang with troops and staff to secure the eastern front.

sentences.zh: 事寧，復為黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉，改領前軍將軍，徙御史中丞，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he again became Yellow Gate Attendant and Infantry Commandant, then changed to Van General, moved to Imperial Censor, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he returned as Yellow Gate Attendant and infantry commandant, then became van general, imperial censor, and finally palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 上以伐逆寧亂，事資羣謀，大明元年，下詔曰：「昔歲國難方結，疑懦者眾，故散騎常侍、太子右率龐秀之履嶮能貞，首暢義節，用使狡狀先聞，軍備夙固，醜逆時殄，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: The emperor, because suppressing rebellion and settling disorder relied on the counsel of many, in the first year of Daming issued an edict saying: "In years past the national peril had just formed and the timid were many; therefore the Palace Attendant and Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household Pang Xiuzhi, treading danger yet able to remain steadfast, first gave voice to righteous principle; thereby the treacherous design was heard of in advance, military preparations were long firm, the ugly rebel was destroyed in time, and he had considerable merit therein.
translations.idiomatic: Because putting down rebellion had depended on many counsellors, in Daming 1 the emperor issued an edict: "When the realm was first imperiled and cowards were everywhere, Pang Xiuzhi, palace attendant and right leader of the heir's household, stood firm in danger and was the first to speak for righteousness. Thanks to him the plot was known in advance, the army was ready, and the rebel was destroyed in good time. He deserves great credit.

sentences.zh: 追念厥誠，無忘于懷。

translations.literal: Recalling his loyalty, we do not forget it in our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We remember his loyalty and hold it ever in mind.

sentences.zh: 侍中祭酒顏師伯、侍中領射聲校尉袁愍孫、豫章太守王謙之、太子前中庶子領右衞率張淹，爰始入討，預參義謀，契闊大難，宜蒙殊報。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Director of Sacrifices Yan Shibo, Palace Attendant and Director of the Sound-Shooting Commandant Yuan Minsun, Administrator of Yuzhang Wang Qianzhi, and Former Right Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household Zhang Yan—from the first entering to attack, they took part in righteous planning; through the great peril they shared, they should receive extraordinary reward.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yan Shibo, palace attendant and sound-shooting commandant Yuan Minsun, Yuzhang governor Wang Qianzhi, and former right guard leader of the heir's household Zhang Yan joined the punitive campaign from the start and shared in the planning. Having endured the crisis together, they deserve exceptional reward.

sentences.zh: 秀之可封樂安縣伯，食邑六百戶，師伯平都縣子，愍孫興平縣子，謙之石陽縣子，淹廣晉縣子，食邑各五百戶。」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi may be enfeoffed as Baron of Le'an County with a fief of six hundred households; Shibo as Viscount of Pingdu County, Minsun as Viscount of Xingping County, Qianzhi as Viscount of Shiyang County, and Yan as Viscount of Guangjin County, each with a fief of five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi shall be made Baron of Le'an with six hundred households; Shibo Viscount of Pingdu, Minsun Viscount of Xingping, Qianzhi Viscount of Shiyang, and Yan Viscount of Guangjin, each with five hundred households."

sentences.zh: 師伯遷右衞將軍，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Shibo was transferred to Right Guard General and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo was promoted to right guard general and left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 二年，起為持節、督青冀二州徐州之東安東莞兗州之濟北三郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three commanderies of Dong'an and Dongguan in Xu Province and Jibei in Yan Province, Country-Aiding General, and Inspector of the two provinces of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as bearer of the staff of authority and commander of forces in Dong'an and Dongguan in Xu and Jibei in Yan, with the rank of country-aiding general and governor of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 其年，索虜拓跋濬遣偽散騎常侍、鎮西將軍天水公拾賁敕文率眾寇清口，清口戍主振威將軍傅乾愛率前員外將軍周盤龍等擊大破之。

translations.literal: That year the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Jun sent the Wei Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the West, Duke of Tianshui Shiben Dewen, leading troops to raid Qingkou; the garrison commander of Qingkou, General Who Stirs Martial Ardor Fu Gan'ai, with Former Staff General Zhou Panlong and others struck and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Wei ruler Tuoba Jun sent his palace attendant and General Who Guards the West, the Duke of Tianshui Shiben Dewen, against Qingkou. Fu Gan'ai, the garrison commander at Qingkou, and Zhou Panlong and others routed the invaders.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣虎賁主龐孟虯、積射將軍殷孝祖等赴討，受師伯節度。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent Tiger Guard Commander Pang Mengjiao, General of Accumulated Shots Yin Xiaozu, and others to pursue the attack, subject to Shibo's command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent Pang Mengjiao of the tiger guard and Yin Xiaozu, general of accumulated shots, among others to join the campaign under Shibo's command.

sentences.zh: 師伯遣中兵參軍苟思達與孟虯合力。

translations.literal: Shibo sent Central Troops Adjutant Gou Sida to join forces with Mengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo dispatched his central troops adjutant Gou Sida to combine forces with Mengjiao.

sentences.zh: 行達沙溝，虜窟瓌公、五軍公等馬步數萬，迎軍拒戰，孟虯等奮擊盡日，孟虯手斬五軍公，虜於是大奔。

translations.literal: Advancing to Shagou, the barbarians' Kulgui Duke, Duke of the Five Armies, and others with tens of thousands of horse and foot met the army and resisted battle; Mengjiao and the others fought fiercely all day; Mengjiao with his own hand beheaded the Duke of the Five Armies, and the barbarians then fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Near Shagou the Wei Kulgui Duke, Duke of the Five Armies, and others met them with tens of thousands of cavalry and infantry. Mengjiao's men fought all day; Mengjiao himself slew the Duke of the Five Armies, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 孝祖又斬窟瓌公，赴水死者千計。

translations.literal: Xiaozu also beheaded Kulgui Duke; those who drowned in the water numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu also killed the Kulgui Duke, and more than a thousand drowned trying to escape across the water.

sentences.zh: 虜又遣河南公、黑水公、濟州公、青州刺史張懷之等屯據濟岸，師伯又遣中兵參軍江方興就傅乾愛擊破之，斬河南公樹蘭等。

translations.literal: The barbarians again sent the Duke of Henan, Duke of Black Water, Duke of Ji Province, and Inspector of Qing Province Zhang Huai Zhi and others to hold the north bank of the Ji; Shibo again sent Central Troops Adjutant Jiang Fangxing with Fu Gan'ai to strike and rout them, beheading the Duke of Henan Shulan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sent the Dukes of Henan, Black Water, and Ji, together with Qing governor Zhang Huai Zhi, to hold the north bank of the Ji. Shibo sent Jiang Fangxing with Fu Gan'ai to defeat them and behead the Duke of Henan Shulan and others.

sentences.zh: 虜別帥它門又遣萬餘人攻清口戍城，乾愛、方興出城拒戰，即斬它門，餘眾奔走。

translations.literal: Another barbarian commander, Tamen, again sent more than ten thousand men to attack the Qingkou garrison city; Gan'ai and Fangxing went out of the city to resist battle and immediately beheaded Tamen; the remaining masses fled.
translations.idiomatic: Another Wei commander, Tamen, sent more than ten thousand men against the Qingkou garrison. Gan'ai and Fangxing sallied forth, killed Tamen at once, and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 虜天水公又率二萬人復來逼城，乾愛等出戰，又破之，追奔至赤龍門，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: The barbarian Duke of Tianshui again led twenty thousand men to press the city; Gan'ai and the others went out to battle and again routed them, pursuing the rout to Chilong Gate and killing very many of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tianshui returned with twenty thousand men to threaten the city. Gan'ai and his officers defeated them again, pursued them to Chilong Gate, and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其功，詔曰：「虜驅率犬羊，規暴邊塞，輔國將軍、青冀二州刺史師伯宣略命師，合變應機，濟戍奮怒，一月四捷，支軍異部，騁勇齊效，頻梟名王，大殲羣醜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised their merit and issued an edict saying: "The barbarians drive herds of dogs and sheep and scheme violence on the frontier; Country-Aiding General and Inspector of the two provinces of Qing and Ji Shibo proclaimed strategy and commanded the army, adapting to change and responding to opportunity; the garrison troops fought in fury, four victories in one month; branch armies of different divisions exerted courage together in effect; repeatedly they beheaded famous princes and greatly slaughtered the rebel masses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended their achievement in an edict: "The barbarians, driving their hordes like dogs and sheep, ravage the frontier. Shibo, country-aiding general and governor of Qing and Ji, deployed his strategy wisely and adapted to events. The garrison troops fought with fury and won four victories in a month. Detached columns from different commands fought side by side, repeatedly slaying Wei princes and crushing the enemy hosts.

sentences.zh: 朕用嘉嘆，良深于懷。

translations.literal: We praise and sigh with admiration, deeply in our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We are deeply moved and full of admiration.

sentences.zh: 可遣使慰勞，并符輔國府詳考功最，以時言上。」

translations.literal: An envoy may be sent to offer consolation, and orders sent to the Country-Aiding headquarters to examine merits in detail and report upward in timely fashion."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to congratulate them, and instruct the country-aiding headquarters to review their merits in full and report promptly."

sentences.zh: 苟思達、龐孟虯等又追虜至杜梁，虜眾多，四面俱合，平南參軍童太壹及苟思達等並單騎出盪，應手披靡。

translations.literal: Gou Sida, Pang Mengjiao, and others again pursued the barbarians to Duliang; the barbarian masses were many and closed in on all four sides; Pacifying South Adjutant Tong Taiyi and Gou Sida and others each rode out alone to charge, and the enemy fell before their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Sida, Pang Mengjiao, and others pursued the enemy to Duliang, where they were surrounded on all sides. Tong Taiyi, Gou Sida, and others charged alone on horseback and cut down all who met them.

sentences.zh: 孟虯等繼至，虜乃散走，透河死者甚多。

translations.literal: Mengjiao and the others arrived in succession; the barbarians then scattered and fled; very many died crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengjiao's reinforcements arrived the enemy broke and ran, and a great many drowned crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 既而虜更合眾大至，孟虯等又破之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the barbarians again combined their masses and came in great force; Mengjiao and the others again routed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei soon gathered a larger force, but Mengjiao and his men defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 世祖又遣司空參軍卜天生助師伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu again sent Staff Officer Bu Tiansheng to assist Shibo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent his staff officer Bu Tiansheng to reinforce Shibo.

sentences.zh: 張懷之據縻溝城，師伯遣天生等破之，懷之出城逆戰，天生率軍主劉懷珍、白衣客朱士義、殿中將軍孟繼祖等擊之。

translations.literal: Zhang Huai Zhi held Micheng; Shibo sent Tiansheng and others to rout him; Huai Zhi went out of the city to meet battle in advance; Tiansheng led Army Commander Liu Huaizhen, plain-clothed retainer Zhu Shiyi, Palace Guard General Meng Jizu, and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huai Zhi held Micheng. Shibo sent Tiansheng against him; Huai Zhi came out to fight, and Tiansheng led Liu Huaizhen, Zhu Shiyi, Meng Jizu, and others into the attack.

sentences.zh: 懷之敗走入城，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Huai Zhi was defeated and fled into the city, barely escaping with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhi was beaten back into the city and barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 繼祖於陳遇害，追贈郡守。

translations.literal: Jizu was killed in battle; posthumously awarded Commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu was killed in the fighting and was posthumously made commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 又虜隴西王等屯據申城，背濟向河，三面險固，天生又率眾攻之，朱士義等貫甲先登，賊赴河死者無算，即日陷城。

translations.literal: Again the barbarian Prince of Longxi and others held Shen City, with their backs to the Ji and facing the river on three sides in dangerous solidity; Tiansheng again led the masses to attack; Zhu Shiyi and others in full armor scaled first; rebels who rushed into the river died beyond counting; the city fell that same day.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Prince of Longxi and others held Shen City, backed by the Ji and fortified on three sides. Tiansheng attacked again; Zhu Shiyi and others scaled the walls in full armor, and so many fell into the river that their deaths could not be counted. The city fell the same day.

sentences.zh: 虜天水公又攻樂安城，建威將軍、平原樂安二郡太守分武都與卜天生等拒擊，大破之，虜乃奔退，追戰克捷，直至清口。

translations.literal: The barbarian Duke of Tianshui again attacked Le'an City; General Who Establishes Martial Ardor and Administrator of the two commanderies of Pingyuan and Le'an Fen Wudu with Bu Tiansheng and others resisted and struck, greatly routing them; the barbarians then fled in retreat; pursuing battle achieved victory straight to Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tianshui attacked Le'an again. Fen Wudu, establishing-martial general and governor of Pingyuan and Le'an, with Bu Tiansheng and others repulsed him, routed the enemy, and pursued in victory all the way to Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 虜攻圍傅乾愛，乾愛隨方拒對，孝祖等既至，虜徹圍遁走。

translations.literal: The barbarians besieged Fu Gan'ai; Gan'ai resisted according to each approach; when Xiaozu and the others arrived, the barbarians lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei besieged Fu Gan'ai, who held them off from every side. When Xiaozu and the others arrived the enemy broke the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 師伯進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Shibo was promoted in rank to General Who Punishes Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo was promoted to general who punishes barbarians.

sentences.zh: 三年，竟陵王誕反，師伯遣長史嵇玄敬率五千人赴難。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Shibo sent Chief of Staff Ji Xuanjing leading five thousand men to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Shibo sent his chief of staff Ji Xuanjing with five thousand men to the relief.

sentences.zh: 四年，徵為侍中，領右軍將軍，親幸隆密，羣臣莫二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Right Army; imperial favor was intimate and dense, and among ministers none was second.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled as palace attendant and director of the right army. The emperor's favor was intimate beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，右軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel and retained the Right Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the masters of writing for personnel while keeping his post with the right army.

sentences.zh: 上不欲威柄在人，親監庶務，前後領選者，唯奉行文書，師伯專情獨斷，奏無不可。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish authority to rest in others' hands and personally oversaw routine affairs; those who previously directed appointments only carried out documents, but Shibo decided matters on his own authority and none of his memorials was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not let power rest in others' hands and kept close watch on daily business. Previous personnel directors had merely processed paperwork, but Shibo decided on his own and every proposal he submitted was approved.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，領右衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Director of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and director of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，補尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was also appointed vice director of the masters of writing on the right.

sentences.zh: 時分置二選，陳郡謝莊、琅邪王曇生並為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At that time appointments were divided into two selections; Xie Zhuang of Chen Commandery and Wang Tansheng of Langya were both Directors of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At that time personnel appointments were split between two directors: Xie Zhuang of Chen and Wang Tansheng of Langya.

sentences.zh: 師伯子舉周旋寒人張奇為公車令，上以奇資品不當，使兼市買丞，以蔡道惠代之。

translations.literal: Shibo's son Ju promoted the low-born Zhang Qi to Director of the Public Chariots; the emperor thought Qi's qualifications unsuitable and had him additionally serve as market-purchase aide, replacing him with Cai Daohui.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo's son Ju pushed through the appointment of Zhang Qi, a man of humble birth, as director of the public chariots. The emperor judged Qi unqualified, made him market-purchase aide instead, and replaced him with Cai Daohui.

sentences.zh: 令史潘道栖、褚道惠、顏禕之、元從夫、任澹之、石道兒、黃難、周公選等抑道惠敕，使奇先到公車，不施行奇兼市買丞事。

translations.literal: Clerks Pan Daoqi, Chu Daohui, Yan Yizhi, Yuan Congfu, Ren Tanzhi, Shi Dao'er, Huang Nan, Zhou Gongxuan, and others suppressed Daohui's order, causing Qi to reach the public chariots first and not carry out Qi's additional duties as market-purchase aide.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks Pan Daoqi, Chu Daohui, Yan Yizhi, Yuan Congfu, Ren Tanzhi, Shi Dao'er, Huang Nan, and Zhou Gongxuan blocked Daohui's appointment so that Qi took the public chariots post first and never served as market-purchase aide.

sentences.zh: 師伯坐以子領職，莊、曇生免官，道栖、道惠棄市，禕之等六人鞭杖一百。

translations.literal: Shibo was punished because his son held office; Zhuang and Tansheng were removed from office; Daoqi and Daohui were executed in the marketplace; Yizhi and the other six men were flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo was punished because his son had secured the post. Zhuang and Tansheng were dismissed, Daoqi and Daohui were executed in the marketplace, and Yizhi and six others were flogged a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 師伯尋領太子中庶子，雖被黜挫，受任如初。

translations.literal: Shibo soon afterward additionally served as Senior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; though demoted and rebuffed, he was entrusted as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo was soon made senior tutor to the heir apparent. Despite the setback, he was entrusted as before.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨崩，師伯受遺詔輔幼主，尚書中事，專以委之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was near death, Shibo received the testamentary edict to assist the young ruler; affairs within the Masters of Writing were entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Xiaowu charged Shibo by testamentary edict to assist the young emperor and left the affairs of the masters of writing entirely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，復還即真，領衞尉。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, Shibo again returned to full appointment and directed the Court of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Shibo resumed full rank and became director of the court of the guard.

sentences.zh: 師伯居權日久，天下輻輳，游其門者，爵位莫不踰分。

translations.literal: Shibo had held power for a long time; the realm converged on him like wheel spokes; those who frequented his gate received ranks none of which failed to exceed proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo had held power for years, and the empire flocked to his door. Those who curried favor with him received offices and titles far above their due.

sentences.zh: 多納貨賄，家產豐積，伎妾聲樂，盡天下之選，園池第宅，冠絕當時，驕奢淫恣，為衣冠所嫉。

translations.literal: He accepted many bribes; his household wealth piled high; singing girls and musicians were chosen from the finest in the realm; gardens, ponds, mansions, and residences surpassed all of the age; arrogant, extravagant, licentious, and unrestrained, he was envied by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes on a vast scale and amassed enormous wealth. His concubines and musicians were the finest in the land, his gardens and mansions the grandest of the age. Proud, extravagant, and dissolute, he was loathed by the gentry.

sentences.zh: 又遷尚書僕射，領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of Danyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made vice director of the masters of writing and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 廢帝欲親朝政，發詔轉師伯為左僕射，加散騎常侍，以吏部尚書王景文為右僕射。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor wished to take charge of court affairs personally and issued an edict transferring Shibo to Left Vice Director and adding Palace Attendant, with Wang Jingwen as Director of the Masters of Writing made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor wanted to govern in person and transferred Shibo to left vice director with the added rank of palace attendant, making Wang Jingwen right vice director.

sentences.zh: 奪其京尹，又分臺任，師伯至是始懼。

translations.literal: He stripped him of the capital prefecture and again divided the secretariat's duties; only then did Shibo begin to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of the capital prefecture and with his secretariat powers divided, Shibo at last grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 尋與太宰江夏王義恭、柳元景同誅，時年四十七。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was executed together with Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and Liu Yuanjing; he was then forty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon executed along with Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and Liu Yuanjing, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 六子並幼，皆見殺。

translations.literal: His six sons were all young and were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: All six of his young sons were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 弟師仲，中書郎，晉陵太守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shizhong was Attendant of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shizhong served as attendant of the masters of writing and governor of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 師叔，司徒主簿，南康相。

translations.literal: Shishu was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works and Administrator of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu was chief clerk to the minister of works and governor of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔曰︰「故散騎常侍、僕射、領丹陽尹、平都縣子師伯，昔逢代運，豫班榮賞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, an edict said: "The late Palace Attendant, Vice Director, Director of Danyang Prefecture, and Viscount of Pingdu County Shibo—in years past met the changing fortune of the age and received rank and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he issued an edict: "The late palace attendant, vice director, governor of Danyang, and Viscount of Pingdu Shibo once rose with the fortunes of the age and received honor and reward.

sentences.zh: 遭罹厄會，隕命淫刑，宗嗣殄絕，良用矜悼。

translations.literal: He met a calamitous turn of fate, lost his life to licentious punishment, and his line was extinguished; we deeply pity and mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: He met a cruel fate, died by arbitrary execution, and his line was cut off. We deeply mourn him.

sentences.zh: 但其心瀆貨，宜貶贈典，可紹封社，以慰寃魂。

translations.literal: Yet his heart was corrupt with goods; the posthumous honors should be reduced; he may receive renewed enfeoffment of the fief to comfort his wronged soul.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because his heart was stained by greed, his posthumous honors should be diminished. Still, let the fief be restored to comfort his wronged spirit.

sentences.zh: 諡曰荒子。」

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Viscount of Recklessness."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Viscount of Recklessness."

sentences.zh: 師仲子幹繼封。

translations.literal: Shizhong's son Gan succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong's son Gan inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi

sentences.zh: 沈慶之字弘先，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi, styled Hongxian, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, whose courtesy name was Hongxian, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄敞之，為趙倫之征虜參軍、監南陽郡，擊蠻有功，遂即真。

translations.literal: His elder brother Changzhi served as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Staff Officer to Zhao Luzhi and as Acting Administrator of Nanyang; he attacked the barbarians with merit and then assumed full office.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Changzhi served on Zhao Luzhi's staff as general-who-pacifies-the-barbarians staff officer and acting governor of Nanyang. His successful campaigns against the barbarians earned him confirmation in the post.

sentences.zh: 慶之少有志力。

translations.literal: Qingzhi in youth had aspiration and strength.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qingzhi possessed resolve and physical strength.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之亂也，遣人寇武康，慶之未冠，隨鄉族擊之，由是以勇聞。

translations.literal: During Sun En's rebellion, Sun En sent men to raid Wukang; Qingzhi had not yet come of age but followed the local clans to attack them, and thereby became known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: During Sun En's rebellion, when raiders struck Wukang, Qingzhi—still before his coming-of-age—joined his kinsmen in driving them off and won a reputation for courage.

sentences.zh: 荒擾之後，鄉邑流散，慶之躬耕壟畝，勤苦自立。

translations.literal: After the desolation and upheaval, the hometown was scattered; Qingzhi personally plowed the fields and through hard labor supported himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the devastation drove the community apart, Qingzhi worked the fields himself and through hardship made his own way.

sentences.zh: 年三十，未知名，往襄陽省兄，倫之見而賞之。

translations.literal: At age thirty, still without renown, he went to Xiangyang to visit his elder brother; Luzhi saw him and appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he was still unknown. When he went to Xiangyang to visit his brother, Luzhi took notice of him and valued his qualities.

sentences.zh: 倫之子伯符時為竟陵太守，倫之命伯符版為寧遠中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Luzhi's son Bofu was then Administrator of Jingling; Luzhi ordered Bofu to appoint him provisionally as General Who Renders Service from Afar Staff Officer for Central Army Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhi's son Bofu was then governor of Jingling, and Luzhi had Bofu provisionally appoint Qingzhi staff officer for central army affairs under the rank of general who renders service from afar.

sentences.zh: 竟陵蠻屢為寇，慶之為設規略，每擊破之，伯符由此致將帥之稱。

translations.literal: The Jingling barbarians repeatedly raided; Qingzhi devised plans for them and each time defeated them, and Bofu thereby gained the reputation of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingling barbarians raided again and again, Qingzhi devised the strategy that broke them each time, and Bofu won repute as a capable commander.

sentences.zh: 伯符去郡，又別討西陵蠻，不與慶之相隨，無功而反。

translations.literal: Bofu left the commandery and separately campaigned against the Xiling barbarians without Qingzhi accompanying him; he returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After Bofu left the post, he mounted a separate campaign against the Xiling barbarians without Qingzhi at his side and came back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，慶之除殿中員外將軍，又隨伯符隸到彥之北伐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, Qingzhi was appointed Supernumerary General of the Palace; he again followed Bofu under Dao Yanzhi's northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 2, Qingzhi was appointed supernumerary general of the palace and again followed Bofu on Dao Yanzhi's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 伯符病歸，仍隸檀道濟。

translations.literal: Bofu fell ill and returned home; Qingzhi still served under Tan Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: When illness sent Bofu home, Qingzhi remained attached to Tan Daoji's command.

sentences.zh: 道濟還白太祖，稱慶之忠謹曉兵，上使領隊防東掖門，稍得引接，出入禁省。

translations.literal: Daoji on returning reported to Emperor Wu, praising Qingzhi as loyal, careful, and knowledgeable in military affairs; the emperor had him lead a guard defending the Eastern Side Gate, gradually obtained patronage access, and enter and leave the forbidden palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Daoji told Emperor Wu that Qingzhi was loyal, conscientious, and skilled in military affairs. The emperor assigned him to lead guards at the eastern side gate, gradually opened paths of advancement for him, and allowed him to enter the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 出戍錢唐新城，及還，領淮陵太守。

translations.literal: He went out to garrison New City in Qiantang; when he returned, he served concurrently as Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: After garrison duty at New City in Qiantang, he returned to serve concurrently as governor of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍劉湛知之，欲相引接，謂之曰：「卿在省年月久，比當相論。」

translations.literal: General Who Controls the Army Liu Zhan learned of this and wished to extend patronage to him, saying to him: "You have been in the palace for many years; it is time to speak on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Zhan, who controlled the army, learned of him and offered his patronage. "You have served at court for years," he said. "It is time I spoke up for you."

sentences.zh: 慶之正色曰：「下官在省十年，自應得轉，不復以此仰累。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi with stern countenance said: "This subordinate official has been in the palace ten years and ought by rights to be transferred; I will no longer rely on others for this."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi answered gravely: "I have served at court for ten years and should be promoted on my own merits. I will not burden you to intervene on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 尋轉正員將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to regular General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to full general.

sentences.zh: 及湛被收之夕，上開門召慶之，慶之戎服履靺縛絝入，上見而驚曰：「卿何意乃爾急裝？」

translations.literal: On the evening when Zhan was arrested, the emperor opened the gate and summoned Qingzhi; Qingzhi entered in military dress wearing leather boots and cross-gartered breeches; the emperor seeing him was startled and said: "Why are you so urgently equipped?"
translations.idiomatic: On the night Liu Zhan was taken into custody, the emperor opened the gates and summoned Qingzhi. Qingzhi entered in full military dress—leather boots and cross-gartered trousers—and the emperor exclaimed in surprise: "Why are you kitted out for battle?"

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「夜半喚隊主，不容緩服。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "At midnight summoning a guard captain allows no time for leisurely dress."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied: "When a guard captain is summoned at midnight, there is no time to change into court dress."

sentences.zh: 遣收吳郡太守劉斌，殺之。

translations.literal: He sent to arrest Liu Bin, Administrator of Wu Commandery, and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Liu Bin, governor of Wu commandery, seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 遷始興王濬後軍行參軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Rear Army Acting Staff Officer to Prince Jun of Shixing and Supernumerary Gentleman of the Dappled Stallions.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as acting rear-army staff officer to Prince Jun of Shixing and supernumerary gentleman attendant at the dappled stallions.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年，雍州刺史劉道產卒，羣蠻大動，征西司馬朱脩之討蠻失利，以慶之為建威將軍，率眾助脩之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, Liu Daochan, Inspector of Yong Province, died; the various barbarians rose in force; Zhu Xiuzhi, General Who Subdues the West Staff Officer, fought the barbarians without success; Qingzhi was made General Who Establishes Might and led troops to assist Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 19, after Yongzhou inspector Liu Daochan died and the barbarians rose in force, Zhu Xiuzhi's campaign against them faltered. Qingzhi was appointed general who establishes might and sent with troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 脩之失律下獄，慶之專軍進討，大破緣沔諸蠻，禽生口七千人。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi violated military discipline and was imprisoned; Qingzhi alone commanded the army in advance attacks, greatly defeated the barbarians along the Han, and captured seven thousand prisoners alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuzhi was jailed for breach of discipline, Qingzhi took sole command, routed the Han River barbarians, and took seven thousand captives alive.

sentences.zh: 進征湖陽，又獲萬餘口。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Huyang, he again took more than ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Huyang, he captured more than ten thousand more.

sentences.zh: 遷廣陵王誕北中郎中兵參軍，領南東平太守，又為世祖撫軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to North Army Staff Officer for Central Troops in the Palace under Prince Dan of Guangling, concurrently served as Administrator of Southern Dongping, and again became Staff Officer for Central Army Affairs under the Heir Apparent's Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to staff officer for central troops under Prince Dan of Guangling's northern army, served concurrently as governor of southern Dongping, and again became central-army staff officer on the heir apparent's pacifying army staff.

sentences.zh: 世祖以本號為雍州，隨府西上。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent took his existing title as Yong Province and Qingzhi followed the office westward.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was assigned Yongzhou under his existing rank, Qingzhi accompanied the establishment west.

sentences.zh: 時蠻寇大甚，水陸梗礙，世祖停大隄不得進。

translations.literal: At that time barbarian raids were severe; land and water routes were blocked; the Heir Apparent halted at the Great Embankment and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raids were then at their worst, blocking both land and water routes, and the heir apparent was stuck at the Great Embankment, unable to advance.

sentences.zh: 分軍遣慶之掩討，大破之，降者二萬口。

translations.literal: He divided the army and sent Qingzhi on a surprise attack; he greatly defeated them, and those who surrendered numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He detached a force under Qingzhi for a surprise campaign that routed the enemy; twenty thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 世祖至鎮，而驛道蠻反殺深式，遣慶之又討之。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent reached his post, barbarians on the courier route rebelled and killed Shen Shi; he sent Qingzhi again to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir apparent reached his post, barbarians along the courier route rebelled and killed Shen Shi. Qingzhi was sent against them once more.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨領荊州，王方回領臺軍並會，平定諸山，獲七萬餘口。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo held Jing Province, Wang Fanghui held the Capital Army, and they joined forces, pacifying the various mountains and taking more than seventy thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo of Jingzhou and Wang Fanghui commanding the capital army joined the campaign, pacified the mountain strongholds, and took more than seventy thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 鄖山蠻最強盛，魯宗之屢討不能克，慶之剪定之，禽三萬餘口。

translations.literal: The Yun Mountain barbarians were strongest; Lu Zongzhi repeatedly attacked them without being able to conquer them; Qingzhi cut them down and pacified them, capturing more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Yun Mountain barbarians were the strongest; Lu Zongzhi had repeatedly failed to subdue them. Qingzhi uprooted them and took more than thirty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 還京師，復為廣陵王誕北中郎中兵參軍，加建威將軍、南濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again became North Army Staff Officer for Central Troops in the Palace under Prince Dan of Guangling, with the added ranks of General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Southern Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, he again served as central-troops staff officer under Prince Dan of Guangling's northern army, with the added titles of general who establishes might and governor of southern Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 雍州蠻又為寇，慶之以將軍、太守復與隨王誕入沔。

translations.literal: The Yong Province barbarians again raided; Qingzhi as general and administrator again entered the Han with Prince Dan of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzhou barbarians raided again, Qingzhi returned to the Han as both general and governor alongside Prince Dan of Sui.

sentences.zh: 既至襄陽，率後軍中兵參軍柳元景、隨郡太守宗慤、振威將軍劉顒、司空參軍魯尚期、安北參軍顧彬、馬文恭、左軍中兵參軍蕭景嗣、前青州別駕崔目連、安蠻參軍劉雍之、奮威將軍王景式等二萬餘人伐沔北諸山蠻，宗慤自新安道入太洪山，元景從均水據五水嶺，文恭出蔡陽口取赤係隖，景式由延山下向赤圻阪，目連、尚期諸軍八道俱進，慶之取五渠，頓破隖以為眾軍節度。

translations.literal: Having reached Xiangyang, he led Rear Army Central Army Staff Officer Liu Yuanjing, Sui Commandery Administrator Zong Que, General Who Rouses Might Liu Yong, Minister of Works Staff Officer Lu Shangqi, Pacifies-the-North Staff Officer Gu Bin, Ma Wengong, Left Army Central Army Staff Officer Xiao Jingsi, former Qing Province Vice Director Cui Mulian, Pacifies-the-Barbarians Staff Officer Liu Yongzhi, General Who Rouses Might Wang Jingshi, and others—more than twenty thousand men—to attack the north-of-the-Han mountain barbarians. Zong Que entered Great Hong Mountain by the Xin'an route; Yuanjing held Wushui Ridge from the Jun River; Wengong took Chixi Bay from Caiyang Pass; Jingshi descended from Yanshan toward Chiqian Slope; Mulian, Shangqi, and the other armies advanced in eight columns; Qingzhi took Wuju, encamped after storming the fort, and served as coordinator for all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he led a force of more than twenty thousand, including Liu Yuanjing, Zong Que, Liu Yong, Lu Shangqi, Gu Bin, Ma Wengong, Xiao Jingsi, Cui Mulian, Liu Yongzhi, Wang Jingshi, and others, against the barbarians north of the Han. Zong Que entered Great Hong Mountain by the Xin'an route; Yuanjing seized Wushui Ridge from the Jun River; Wengong struck Chixi Bay from Caiyang Pass; Jingshi descended from Yanshan toward Chiqian Slope; Mulian, Shangqi, and the rest advanced in eight columns. Qingzhi took Wuju, broke the fort, and made camp as overall coordinator of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 前後伐蠻，皆山下安營以迫之，故蠻得據山為阻，於矢石有用，以是屢無功。

translations.literal: In barbarian campaigns before and after, all encamped below the mountains to press them, so the barbarians could use the mountains as barriers where arrows and stones were effective, and for this reason were repeatedly without success.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier campaigns had always camped at the foot of the mountains to press the enemy, which let the barbarians hold the heights where arrows and rolling stones were deadly. That was why previous efforts had failed.

sentences.zh: 慶之乃會諸軍於茹丘山下，謂眾曰：「今若緣山列斾以攻之，則士馬必損。

translations.literal: Qingzhi then assembled the armies below Ruqiu Mountain and said to the multitude: "If now we array banners along the mountain to attack, then men and horses will surely suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi gathered the commanders below Ruqiu Mountain and told them: "If we deploy our banners along the slopes to attack, our men and horses will suffer heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 去歲蠻田大稔，積穀重巖，未有饑弊，卒難禽剪。

translations.literal: Last year the barbarians' fields had a great harvest; grain was stored in layered cliffs; there was not yet hunger and exhaustion; it will be hard to capture and cut them down in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's harvest had filled their cliffside granaries. They are not yet hungry or weakened, so a quick strike will not destroy them.

sentences.zh: 今令諸軍各率所領以營于山上，出其不意，諸蠻必恐，恐而乘之，可不戰而獲也。」

translations.literal: Now order the various armies each to lead their commands to encamp on the mountains, taking them unawares; the various barbarians will surely fear; fear them and seize the moment, and without fighting we can capture them."
translations.idiomatic: Order every unit to encamp on the heights with their full strength, catching them off guard. Terror will break them—and terror is the moment to strike. We can take them without a pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍並斬山開道，不與蠻戰，鼓譟上山，衝其腹心，先據險要，諸蠻震擾，因其懼而圍之，莫不奔潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various armies all cut mountains and opened paths, did not battle the barbarians, beat drums and clamored up the mountains, struck their inner core, first seized strategic points; the various barbarians were shaken and disturbed; taking advantage of their fear they surrounded them, and none did not flee in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The armies cut paths through the slopes without engaging the barbarians directly. Beating drums and shouting, they stormed the heights, seized the strong points at the heart of the enemy positions, and threw the barbarians into panic. While terror still held them, the encirclement closed and they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 自冬至春，因糧蠻穀。

translations.literal: From winter to spring, they relied on barbarian grain for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: From winter through spring they subsisted on grain captured from the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 頃之，南新郡蠻帥田彥生率部曲十封六千餘人反叛，攻圍郡城，慶之遣元景率五千人赴之。

translations.literal: Before long, the barbarian chieftain Tian Yansheng of Nanxin Commandery led his command, ten feng, and more than six thousand men in rebellion, attacked and besieged the commandery city; Qingzhi sent Yuanjing to lead five thousand men to go to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Nanxin barbarian chieftain Tian Yansheng rebelled at the head of more than six thousand followers in ten clan divisions, besieging the commandery seat. Qingzhi dispatched Yuanjing with five thousand men to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 軍未至，郡已被破，焚燒城內倉儲及廨舍蕩盡，并驅略降戶，屯據白楊山。

translations.literal: Before the army arrived, the commandery had already been taken; they burned the city storehouses and government offices until nothing remained, also drove and plundered surrendered households, and encamped holding White Poplar Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Before relief arrived the city had fallen. The rebels burned the granaries and government buildings to the ground, drove off surrendered households as booty, and fortified themselves on White Poplar Mountain.

sentences.zh: 元景追之至山下，眾軍悉集，圍山數重。

translations.literal: Yuanjing pursued them to below the mountain; the multitudes of armies all assembled and surrounded the mountain in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing pursued them to the mountain's base. All units converged and ringed the heights in layer upon layer.

sentences.zh: 宗慤率其所領先登，眾軍齊力急攻，大破之，威震諸山，羣蠻皆稽顙。

translations.literal: Zong Que led his command in first ascent; the multitudes of armies with combined strength pressed the attack and greatly defeated them; authority shook the various mountains; the various barbarians all kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Que's men scaled the heights first; the combined force stormed the position and broke it utterly. The victory terrified every mountain stronghold, and the barbarian leaders submitted with foreheads to the ground.

sentences.zh: 慶之患頭風，好著狐皮帽，羣蠻惡之，號曰「蒼頭公」。

translations.literal: Qingzhi suffered from headaches and liked to wear a fox-fur hat; the various barbarians hated it and called him "Lord Dark-Head."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi suffered from migraines and habitually wore a fox-fur cap. The barbarians loathed the sight and called him "Lord Dark-Head."

sentences.zh: 每見慶之軍，輒畏懼曰：「蒼頭公已復來矣。」

translations.literal: Whenever they saw Qingzhi's army, they immediately feared and said: "Lord Dark-Head has come again."
translations.idiomatic: At the sight of his troops they would cry in terror: "Lord Dark-Head is back!"

sentences.zh: 慶之引軍自茹丘山出檢城，大破諸山，斬首三千級，虜生蠻二萬八千餘口，降蠻二萬五千口，牛馬七百餘頭，米粟九萬餘斛。

translations.literal: Qingzhi led the army out from Ruqiu Mountain through Jiancheng, greatly defeated the various mountains, beheaded three thousand, captured barbarians alive more than twenty-eight thousand, barbarians who surrendered twenty-five thousand, cattle and horses more than seven hundred head, and rice and grain more than ninety thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi led his army from Ruqiu Mountain through Jiancheng and crushed the mountain strongholds: three thousand heads taken, more than twenty-eight thousand captives, twenty-five thousand who surrendered, over seven hundred head of cattle and horses, and more than ninety thousand bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕築納降、受俘二城於白楚。

translations.literal: Prince Dan of Sui built two cities, Accepting Surrenders and Receiving Captives, at Baichu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Sui built two settlements at Baichu—Accepting Surrenders and Receiving Captives—to hold the newly subdued population.

sentences.zh: 慶之復率眾軍討幸諸山犬羊蠻，緣險築重城，施門櫓，甚峻。

translations.literal: Qingzhi again led the multitudes of armies to attack the various mountains' dog-and-sheep barbarians; along precipices they built layered fortifications, set gate towers and watchtowers, very steep.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi again led the combined armies against the "dog-and-sheep" barbarians of the mountain ranges. They had built tiered fortresses along the cliffs, with gate towers and watchtowers—formidable defenses.

sentences.zh: 山多木石，積以為礧。

translations.literal: The mountains had much wood and stone, piled to serve as rolling obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: Timber and stone abounded on the slopes, stockpiled as rolling weapons.

sentences.zh: 立部曲，建旌旗，樹長帥，鐵馬成羣。

translations.literal: They established commands, raised banners and flags, set up chieftains, and iron horses formed groups.
translations.idiomatic: They had organized their fighters, raised banners, appointed chieftains, and massed cavalry in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 慶之連營山下，營中開門相通，又命諸軍各穿池於營內，朝夕不外汲，兼以防蠻之火。

translations.literal: Qingzhi linked camps below the mountain; within the camps gates opened connecting to one another; he also ordered the various armies each to dig pools within the camps so morning and evening they need not draw water outside, also to guard against barbarian fire.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi linked his camps at the mountain's foot, connecting them with internal gates. He ordered each unit to dig pools inside its camp so troops never had to leave for water—and to douse any night attack by fire.

sentences.zh: 頃之風甚，蠻夜下山，人提一炬以燒營。

translations.literal: Before long the wind was strong; at night the barbarians came down the mountain, each person carrying one torch to burn the camps.
translations.idiomatic: When a strong wind rose, the barbarians descended at night, each man carrying a torch to set the camps ablaze.

sentences.zh: 營內多幔屋及草菴，火至輒以池水灌滅，諸軍多出弓弩夾射之，蠻散走。

translations.literal: Within the camps were many tent dwellings and grass huts; when fire arrived they immediately used pool water to pour and extinguish; the various armies mostly sent out crossbows to shoot from both sides, and the barbarians scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Canvas tents and grass huts filled the camps, but as flames spread the pools supplied water to douse them. Archers volleyed from every side and the barbarians broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 慶之令諸軍斬山開道攻之，而山高路險，暑雨方盛，乃置東岡、蜀山、宜民、西柴、黃徼、上夌六戍而還。

translations.literal: Qingzhi ordered the various armies to cut mountains and open paths to attack; but the mountains were high and roads perilous, summer rains were then heavy, and he established six garrisons—East Mound, Shu Mountain, Benefits-the-People, West Firewood, Yellow Outpost, and Upper Ling—and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi ordered his forces to cut paths up the slopes and attack, but the heights were steep and summer rains swelled. He established six garrisons—East Mound, Shu Mountain, Benefits-the-People, West Firewood, Yellow Outpost, and Upper Ling—and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蠻被圍守日久，並饑乏，自後稍出歸降。

translations.literal: The barbarians having been besieged and guarded for a long time were all hungry and exhausted; from then on they gradually came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off and besieged for months, the barbarians grew hungry and weak and gradually came down to surrender.

sentences.zh: 慶之前後所獲蠻，並移京邑，以為營戶。

translations.literal: The barbarians Qingzhi captured before and after were all moved to the capital region to serve as military-camp households.
translations.idiomatic: All the barbarians Qingzhi had taken, in campaign after campaign, were resettled in the capital region as military households.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was transferred to Commandant of Foot Soldiers of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he was promoted to commandant of the crown prince's foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其年，太祖將北討，慶之諫曰：「馬步不敵，為日已久矣。

translations.literal: That year, Emperor Wu planned a northern expedition; Qingzhi remonstrated saying: "Cavalry and infantry are not matched; this has been so for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Emperor Wu prepared a northern campaign, Qingzhi remonstrated: "Our infantry and cavalry have long been no match for theirs.

sentences.zh: 請舍遠事，且以檀、到言之。

translations.literal: Please set aside distant affairs and speak with Tan and Dao as examples.
translations.idiomatic: Leave distant schemes aside and consider Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 道濟再行無功，彥之失利而返。

translations.literal: Daoji on two campaigns had no achievement; Yanzhi met defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji campaigned twice without success; Yanzhi was defeated and driven back.

sentences.zh: 今料王玄謨等未踰兩將，六軍之盛，不過往時。

translations.literal: Now estimating Wang Xuemo and others do not surpass the two generals; the six armies' strength does not exceed former times.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo and the rest are no better than those two commanders, and this grand army is no stronger than before.

sentences.zh: 將恐重辱王師，難以得志。」

translations.literal: I fear again shaming the imperial army; it will be hard to achieve one's aim."
translations.idiomatic: I fear we will only disgrace the imperial army again and fail to achieve our aims."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「小醜竊據，河南修復，王師再屈，自別有以；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A petty villain has seized and occupied; Henan is being restored; the imperial army has twice been humbled—for separate reasons;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "A petty foe holds stolen ground and Henan is being restored. The imperial army has twice been humbled—but for reasons of its own.

sentences.zh: 亦由道濟養寇自資，彥之中塗疾動。

translations.literal: Also because Daoji nourished the enemy to enrich himself, and Yanzhi's illness flared mid-journey.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji fattened the enemy for his own gain, and Yanzhi fell ill on the march.

sentences.zh: 虜所恃唯馬，夏水浩汗，河水流通，泛舟北指，則碻磝必走，滑臺小戍，易可覆拔。

translations.literal: What the enemy relies on is only horses; summer waters are vast and surging, the Yellow River flows freely; rowing boats northward, then Que'ao will surely flee, and Huatai, a small garrison, can easily be overturned and taken.
translations.idiomatic: They rely on cavalry alone. With summer floods swelling the rivers, we can sail north—Que'ao will flee, and the small garrison at Huatai will fall easily.

sentences.zh: 克此二戍，館穀弔民，虎牢、洛陽，自然不固。

translations.literal: Capturing these two garrisons, storing grain and comforting the people, Hulao and Luoyang will naturally not hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Once those two posts fall and we stock grain and succor the people, Hulao and Luoyang will not hold.

sentences.zh: 比及冬間，城守相接，虜馬過河，便成禽也。」

translations.literal: By winter, city garrisons linking together, when enemy horses cross the river, they will become captives."
translations.idiomatic: By winter our garrisons will link the line. When their horses cross the river, they will be ours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 慶之又固陳不可。

translations.literal: Qingzhi again firmly stated it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi pressed his objections all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹徐湛之、吏部尚書江湛並在坐，上使湛之等難慶之，慶之曰：「治國譬如治家，耕當問奴，織當訪婢。

translations.literal: Danyang Prefect Xu Zhanzhi and Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zhan were both seated; the emperor had Zhanzhi and others challenge Qingzhi; Qingzhi said: "Governing the state is like governing a household: in plowing one should ask the slave, in weaving one should consult the maid.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang governor Xu Zhanzhi and personnel director Jiang Zhan were present. The emperor had them debate Qingzhi, who said: "Governing a state is like running a household: ask the plowman about farming and the weaver about cloth.

sentences.zh: 陛下今欲伐國，而與白面書生輩謀之，事何由濟。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty now wishes to attack a state yet plots it with pale-faced scholar types—how can the affair succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty means to make war yet plans it with pale-faced scholars. How can such an enterprise succeed?"

sentences.zh: 上大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 及北討，慶之副玄謨向碻磝，戍主棄城走，玄謨圍滑臺，慶之與蕭斌留碻磝，仍領斌輔國司馬。

translations.literal: When the northern expedition came, Qingzhi assisted Xuemo toward Que'ao; the garrison commander abandoned the city and fled; Xuemo besieged Huatai; Qingzhi and Xiao Bin remained at Que'ao, and still served as Bin's Pacifies-the-State Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern campaign began, Qingzhi marched with Xuemo toward Que'ao. The garrison commander fled. Xuemo besieged Huatai while Qingzhi and Xiao Bin held Que'ao, with Qingzhi serving as Bin's pacifies-the-state staff officer.

sentences.zh: 玄謨攻滑臺，積旬不拔。

translations.literal: Xuemo attacked Huatai; for more than ten days he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo besieged Huatai for weeks without success.

sentences.zh: 虜主拓跋燾率大眾南向，斌遣慶之率五千人救玄謨。

translations.literal: The barbarian ruler Tuoba Tao led a great host southward; Bin sent Qingzhi to lead five thousand men to rescue Xuemo.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor Tuoba Tao marched south with a great army. Bin sent Qingzhi with five thousand men to relieve Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「玄謨兵疲眾老，虜寇已逼，各軍營萬人，乃可進耳，少軍輕往，必無益也。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Xuemo's troops are weary and the force aged; the barbarian enemy already presses close; each army camp of ten thousand men—only then can one advance; a small force going lightly will surely be without benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said: "Xuemo's army is exhausted, and the enemy is upon us. We need ten thousand men from every camp before we advance. A token force will do no good."

sentences.zh: 斌固遣令去，會玄謨退，斌將斬之，慶之固諫乃止。

translations.literal: Bin still ordered him to go; it happened that Xuemo retreated; Bin was about to behead him; Qingzhi firmly remonstrated and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bin insisted he go anyway. When Xuemo retreated, Bin would have executed him—but Qingzhi's urgent plea stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖後問：「何故諫斌殺玄謨？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu later asked: "Why did you remonstrate against Bin killing Xuemo?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu asked: "Why did you stop Bin from executing Xuemo?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「諸將奔退，莫不懼罪，自歸而死，將至逃散。

translations.literal: He replied: "The various generals in flight retreat—none do not fear punishment; if one returns to be killed, the generals will come to scatter and flee.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Every retreating officer fears punishment. If returning means death, they will flee and never rally.

sentences.zh: 且大兵至，未宜自弱，故以攻為便耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover when a great army arrives, one should not weaken oneself; therefore taking the offensive is expedient."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when a great army is at hand you must not weaken yourself. The offensive was the practical course."

sentences.zh: 蕭斌以前驅敗績，欲死固碻磝，慶之曰：「夫深入寇境，規求所欲，退敗如此，何可久住。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin because the vanguard was defeated wished to die defending Que'ao firmly; Qingzhi said: "Having deeply entered enemy territory seeking what one desires, retreating in defeat like this—how can one long remain?
translations.idiomatic: After the vanguard's defeat, Xiao Bin wanted to hold Que'ao to the death. Qingzhi said: "We marched deep into enemy territory to seize our objective. After a defeat like this, how can we stay?

sentences.zh: 今青、冀虛弱，而坐守窮城，若虜眾東過，清東非國家有也。

translations.literal: Now Qing and Ji are empty and weak; yet sitting guarding an impoverished city—if the enemy host passes east, Qing-east will not belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Ji provinces lie defenseless. If we sit in this isolated fortress while the enemy sweeps east, the eastern heartland will be lost.

sentences.zh: 碻磝孤絕，復作朱脩之滑臺耳。」

translations.literal: Que'ao is isolated and cut off—again becoming Zhu Xiuzhi's Huatai."
translations.idiomatic: Que'ao is another Huatai—the trap that swallowed Zhu Xiuzhi."

sentences.zh: 會詔使至，不許退，諸將並謂宜留，斌復問計於慶之，慶之曰：「閫外之事，將所得專，詔從遠來，事勢已異。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict messenger arrived, not permitting retreat; the various generals all said one should remain; Bin again asked Qingzhi for a plan; Qingzhi said: "Affairs outside the gate—generals have what they may decide alone; the edict comes from afar—the situation has already changed.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial messenger arrived forbidding retreat. The other generals urged Bin to stay. When Bin asked Qingzhi again, he said: "A field commander decides affairs beyond the frontier. That edict came from far away; the situation has already changed.

sentences.zh: 節下有一范增而不能用，空議何施。」

translations.literal: Under your command there is a Fan Zeng yet you cannot use him—empty discussion, what use?"
translations.idiomatic: You have your own Fan Zeng and will not heed him. Of what use is talk?"

sentences.zh: 斌及坐者並笑曰：「沈公乃更學問。」

translations.literal: Bin and those seated all laughed saying: "Master Shen has turned scholar after all."
translations.idiomatic: Bin and everyone present laughed: "So Marshal Shen has gone literary on us."

sentences.zh: 慶之厲聲曰：「眾人雖見古今，不如下官耳學也。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi in stern voice said: "The multitude though has seen antiquity and the present—is not equal to this subordinate official's learning by ear."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi thundered: "You may have read history, but living experience counts for more than books—and that is where I stand."

sentences.zh: 玄謨自以退敗，求戍碻磝，斌乃還歷城，申坦、垣護之共據清口。

translations.literal: Xuemo because of his own retreat defeat requested to garrison Que'ao; Bin then returned to Licheng; Shen Tan and Yuan Huzhi together held Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo, shamed by his retreat, asked to hold Que'ao. Bin withdrew to Licheng while Shen Tan and Yuan Huzhi held Qingkou together.

sentences.zh: 慶之乘驛馳歸，未至，上驛詔止之，使還救玄謨。

translations.literal: Qingzhi rode post-horses galloping home; before he arrived, an imperial post-station edict stopped him and ordered him to return to rescue Xuemo.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi raced post-horses toward the capital, but before he arrived an imperial courier ordered him to turn back and save Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 會虜已至彭城，不得向北，太尉江夏王義恭留領府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: It happened the enemy had already reached Pengcheng; he could not go north; Grand Commandant Prince Yigong of Jiangxia retained him as Concurrent Staff Officer for Palace Troops.
translations.idiomatic: By then the enemy had reached Pengcheng and the northern route was closed. Grand Commandant Prince Yigong of Jiangxia kept him on as palace-troops staff officer.

sentences.zh: 拓跋燾至卯山，義恭遣慶之率三千拒之，慶之以為虜眾強，往必見禽，不肯行。

translations.literal: Tuoba Tao reached Maoshan; Yigong sent Qingzhi to lead three thousand to resist him; Qingzhi thought the enemy host strong, going would surely mean capture, and refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Tao reached Maoshan, Yigong ordered Qingzhi to block him with three thousand men. Qingzhi judged the enemy too strong—a march out meant capture—and refused.

sentences.zh: 太祖後謂之曰：「河上處分，皆合事宜，惟恨不棄碻磝耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu later said to him: "Dispositions on the river all matched what was fitting; only regretting not abandoning Que'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu told him: "Your dispositions along the river were all sound—my only regret is that Que'ao was not abandoned sooner.

sentences.zh: 卿在左右久，偏解我意，正復違詔濟事，亦無嫌也。」

translations.literal: You have been at my side long and especially understand my intent; even going against the edict to accomplish the affair—there is no offense."
translations.idiomatic: You have been at my side long enough to know my mind. Even when you defied my orders to save the situation, I hold no grievance."

sentences.zh: 二十八年，使慶之自彭城徙流民數千家於瓜步，征北參軍程天祚徙江西流民於南州，亦如之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Qingzhi was ordered to move several thousand displaced households from Pengcheng to Guabu; Northern Expedition Staff Officer Cheng Tianzuo moved displaced households west of the river to Southern Province, likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 Qingzhi resettled several thousand refugee households from Pengcheng to Guabu. Northern campaign staff officer Cheng Tianzuo relocated refugees west of the Yangzi to the southern provinces in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，復更北伐，慶之固諫不從，以立議不同，不使北出。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, again a northern expedition was mounted; Qingzhi firmly remonstrated but was not heeded; because his counsel differed, he was not sent north.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 another northern campaign was planned. Qingzhi remonstrated in vain; because his advice had been rejected before, he was kept from the northern front.

sentences.zh: 是時亡命司馬黑石、廬江叛吏夏侯方進在西陽五水，誑動羣蠻，自淮、汝至于江沔，咸罹其患。

translations.literal: At that time the outlaw Sima Heishi and Lujiang rebel official Xiahou Fangjin were at Xiyang Wushui, deceiving and stirring the various barbarians; from the Huai and Ru to the Jiang and Han, all suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaws Sima Heishi and the Lujiang renegade Xiahou Fangjin were then stirring barbarian revolts from Xiyang's Five Waters. From the Huai and Ru to the Yangzi and Han, the region suffered their raids.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣慶之督諸將討之，詔豫、荊、雍並遣軍，受慶之節度。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Qingzhi was sent to supervise the various generals in attacking them; an edict ordered Yu, Jing, and Yong each to dispatch armies subject to Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Qingzhi was dispatched to command the campaign. Edicts ordered Yu, Jing, and Yong provinces each to send troops under his authority.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，世祖出次五洲，總統羣帥，慶之從巴水出至五洲，諮受軍略。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year, Emperor Xiaowu went out and halted at Wuzhou, overall directing the multitude of commanders; Qingzhi came out from the Ba River to Wuzhou and consulted on and received military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 30 Emperor Xiaowu took up position at Wuzhou to command the generals. Qingzhi marched from the Ba River to Wuzhou to receive his strategy.

sentences.zh: 會世祖典籤董元嗣自京師還，陳元凶弒逆，世祖遣慶之還山引諸軍，慶之謂腹心曰：「蕭斌婦人不足數，其餘將帥，並是所悉，皆易與耳。

translations.literal: It happened Emperor Xiaowu's palace clerk Dong Yuansi returned from the capital and reported the crown prince's regicide; the emperor sent Qingzhi back into the mountains to lead the armies; Qingzhi said to his inner circle: "Xiao Bin is a woman not worth counting; the rest of the commanders are all known to me, all easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: When palace clerk Dong Yuansi arrived from the capital with news of the crown prince's regicide, Emperor Xiaowu sent Qingzhi back into the hills to rally the armies. Qingzhi told his confidants: "Xiao Bin counts for nothing. The rest of the commanders I know well—they will not be hard to handle.

sentences.zh: 東宮同惡不過三十人，此外屈逼，必不為用力。

translations.literal: Those in the Eastern Palace sharing evil are no more than thirty men; beyond them, those coerced will surely not exert effort.
translations.idiomatic: No more than thirty men in the eastern palace truly share his crime. The rest were coerced and will not fight in earnest.

sentences.zh: 今輔順討逆，不憂不濟也。」

translations.literal: Now assisting the compliant to punish the rebellious—there is no worry of not succeeding."
translations.idiomatic: With righteousness on our side against rebellion, success is assured."

sentences.zh: 眾軍既集，假慶之征虜將軍、武昌內史，領府司馬。
