translations.literal: When the armies had assembled, Qingzhi was given acting appointment as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Interior Governor of Wuchang, and concurrently served as headquarters staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armies had gathered, Qingzhi was provisionally named General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and interior governor of Wuchang, and served concurrently as staff officer of the prince's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 世祖還至尋陽，慶之及柳元景等並以天下無主，勸世祖即大位，不許。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu returned to Xunyang, Qingzhi and Liu Yuanjing and others, because the realm had no ruler, all urged Xiaowu to take the great throne; he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu returned to Xunyang, Qingzhi and Liu Yuanjing and the others, seeing the throne vacant, urged him to ascend. He refused.

sentences.zh: 賊劭遣慶之門生錢無忌齎書說慶之解甲，慶之執無忌白世祖。

translations.literal: The rebel Shao sent Qingzhi's former pupil Qian Wuji bearing a letter to persuade Qingzhi to lay down armor; Qingzhi seized Wuji and reported to Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The usurper Shao sent Qingzhi's old protégé Qian Wuji with a letter urging him to disarm. Qingzhi seized Wuji and reported the matter to Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，以慶之為領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，尋出為使持節、督南兗豫徐兗四州諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、南兗州刺史，常侍如故，鎮盱眙。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu ascended the throne, he made Qingzhi General of the Palace Garrison and added Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; soon he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Southern Yanzhou, Yu, Xu, and Yanzhou, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, attendant as before, garrisoning Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu took the throne he made Qingzhi general of the palace garrison and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry. Soon Qingzhi was posted as bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Southern Yanzhou, Yu, Xu, and Yanzhou, general who pacifies the army, and governor of Southern Yanzhou—keeping his attendant rank—stationed at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 上伐逆定亂，思將帥之功，下詔曰：「朕以不天，有生罔二，泣血千里，志復深逆，鞠旅伐罪，義氣雲踴，羣帥仗節，指難如歸。

translations.literal: The emperor, having suppressed rebellion and settled turmoil, mindful of the generals' merits, issued an edict saying: "I, bereft of Heaven's favor in my father, from birth had none other; I wept blood for a thousand li, resolved to avenge this profound treason; I marshaled troops to punish crime; righteous spirit surged like clouds; the commanders, bearing credentials, faced hardship as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Having crushed rebellion and restored order, the emperor wished to honor his commanders and issued an edict: "Heaven took my father while I was young; I had no other to call my own. I wept my way a thousand li to avenge this deepest treason, mustered armies to punish the guilty, and watched righteous valor surge like clouds. My generals took up their staffs and met hardship as men returning home.

sentences.zh: 故曾未積旬，宗社載穆，遂以眇身，猥纂大統。

translations.literal: Thus in less than ten days the altars of state were secured in peace; with my insignificant person I have presumptuously succeeded to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days the altars of state were secure again. With my humble self I have presumptuously inherited the throne.

sentences.zh: 永念茂庸，思崇徽錫。

translations.literal: Ever mindful of great merits, I think to raise high honors and bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful always of their great service, I mean to raise their honors and reward them fittingly.

sentences.zh: 新除使持節、散騎常侍、都督南兗豫徐兗四州諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、南兗州刺史沈慶之，新除散騎常侍、領軍將軍柳元景，新除散騎常侍、右衞將軍宗慤，督兗州諸軍事、輔國將軍、兗州刺史徐遺寶，寧朔將軍、始興太守沈法系，驃騎諮議參軍顧彬之，或盡誠謀初，宣綜戎略；

translations.literal: The newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Southern Yanzhou, Yu, Xu, and Yanzhou, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, Shen Qingzhi; the newly appointed Regular Attendant and General of the Palace Garrison Liu Yuanjing; the newly appointed Regular Attendant and General of the Right Guard Zong Que; Supervisor of Yanzhou Military Affairs, General Who Supports the State, and Governor of Yanzhou Xu Yibao; General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Shixing Shen Faxue; and Staff Officer for Counsel of the General Who Cavalry General, Gu Binzhi—some gave full loyalty in the first planning and deployed the overall military strategy;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, newly appointed bearer of the staff, regular attendant, director of military affairs in Southern Yanzhou, Yu, Xu, and Yanzhou, general who pacifies the army, and governor of Southern Yanzhou; Liu Yuanjing, newly appointed regular attendant and general of the palace garrison; Zong Que, newly appointed regular attendant and general of the right guard; Xu Yibao, supervisor of Yanzhou military affairs, general who supports the state, and governor of Yanzhou; Shen Faxue, general who pacifies the north and governor of Shixing; and Gu Binzhi, staff officer for counsel under the general who cavalry general—some gave their full loyalty from the first planning and shaped the overall strategy;

sentences.zh: 或受命元帥，一戰寧亂；

translations.literal: some received orders from the supreme commander and in one battle restored order;
translations.idiomatic: some took orders from the supreme commander and ended the turmoil in a single battle;

sentences.zh: 或禀奇軍統，協規効捷，偏師奉律，勢振東南。

translations.literal: some received extraordinary military command, cooperated in strategy for swift success, and with detached forces upheld discipline—their momentum shook the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: some commanded exceptional troops, coordinated plans for swift victory, and with detached columns upheld discipline until their momentum shook the southeast.

sentences.zh: 皆忠國忘身，義高前烈，功載民聽，誠簡朕心。

translations.literal: All were loyal to the state and forgot themselves; their righteousness exceeded former exemplars; their deeds are recorded in what the people hear; their sincerity moves my heart.
translations.idiomatic: All forgot themselves for the state. Their loyalty outshone the heroes of old, their deeds are known to the people, and their sincerity speaks directly to my heart.

sentences.zh: 定賞策勳，茲焉攸在，宜列土開邑，永蕃皇家。

translations.literal: To fix rewards and record merit—here is where it lies. It is fitting to grant fiefs and open estates, to be eternal bulwarks of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: To fix rewards and record merit is precisely the purpose of this decree. Let them receive fiefs and open estates as everlasting pillars of the throne.

sentences.zh: 慶之可封南昌縣公，元景曲江縣公，並食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Qingzhi may be enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang county; Yuanjing as Duke of Qujiang county—each with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi shall be enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang with a fief of three thousand households; Yuanjing as Duke of Qujiang with the same.

sentences.zh: 慤洮陽縣侯，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Que as Marquis of Taoyang county, fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Que shall be marquis of Taoyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遺寶益陽縣侯，食邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: Yibao as Marquis of Yiyang county, fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yibao shall be marquis of Yiyang with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 法系平固縣侯，彬之陽新縣侯，並食邑千戶。」

translations.literal: Faxue as Marquis of Pinggu county; Binzhi as Marquis of Yangxin county—each with fiefs of one thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Faxue shall be marquis of Pinggu and Binzhi marquis of Yangxin, each with a fief of one thousand households."

sentences.zh: 又特臨軒召拜。

translations.literal: The emperor also personally summoned them before the palace hall for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He also had them summoned to a special audience in the palace hall for formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 又使慶之自盱眙還鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: He also ordered Qingzhi to return from Xuyi and garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Qingzhi back from Xuyi to garrison Guangling.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年正月，魯爽反，上遣左衞將軍王玄謨討之，軍泝淮向壽陽，總統諸將。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xiaojian, Lu Shuang rebelled; the emperor sent General of the Left Guard Wang Xuemo to suppress him; the army went up the Huai toward Shouyang and exercised overall command of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xiaojian 454, Lu Shuang rebelled. The emperor sent General of the Left Guard Wang Xuemo against him. The army moved up the Huai toward Shouyang, with Xuemo in overall command.

sentences.zh: 尋聞荊、江二州並反，徵慶之入朝，率所領屯武帳崗，甲仗五十人入六門。

translations.literal: Soon word came that Jing and Jiang provinces had both rebelled; Qingzhi was summoned to court, leading his forces to encamp at Wuzhang Ridge, with fifty armed men permitted entry through the six gates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reports arrived that Jing and Jiang provinces had both risen. Qingzhi was recalled to court, camped his troops at Wuzhang Ridge, and was allowed fifty armed men through the six palace gates.

sentences.zh: 魯爽先遣弟瑜進據蒙蘢，歷陽太守張幼緒率軍討瑜，值爽至，眾散而反。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang first sent his younger brother Yu to advance and seize Menglong; Zhang Youxu, Governor of Liyang, led troops against Yu; when Shuang arrived, the force scattered and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang first sent his brother Yu to seize Menglong. Liyang governor Zhang Youxu marched against Yu, but when Shuang himself arrived the force broke and fell back.

sentences.zh: 乃遣慶之濟江討爽。

translations.literal: Then Qingzhi was sent across the river to attack Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was then sent across the river to attack Shuang.

sentences.zh: 爽聞慶之至，連營稍退，自留斷後。

translations.literal: When Shuang heard Qingzhi had arrived, his linked camps gradually withdrew; he himself remained behind as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Qingzhi had come, Shuang began pulling his camps back in stages while he himself stayed behind as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 慶之與薛安都等進與爽戰，安都臨陣斬爽。

translations.literal: Qingzhi with Xue Andu and others advanced to battle Shuang; Andu beheaded Shuang on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi advanced with Xue Andu and the others to give battle. Andu cut Shuang down on the field.

sentences.zh: 進慶之號鎮北大將軍，進督青、冀、幽三州，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Qingzhi was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, given supervision of Qing, Ji, and You provinces, and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was promoted to general who pacifies the north, given supervision of Qing, Ji, and You provinces, and granted a full martial band.

sentences.zh: 前軍破賊，轉位等後至追躡一階。

translations.literal: For vanguard forces that broke the enemy, those who arrived later in rank and title were advanced one step in pursuit credit.
translations.idiomatic: Because the vanguard had broken the enemy, those who arrived later received one step of promotion in rank when the pursuit was credited.

sentences.zh: 尋與柳元景俱開府儀同三司，辭。

translations.literal: Soon he and Liu Yuanjing were both granted Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Liu Yuanjing were both granted grand prefect honors equal to the three excellencies. Qingzhi declined.

sentences.zh: 改封始興郡公，戶邑如故。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Shixing commandery; his fief households remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Shixing commandery while his fief households remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 慶之以年滿七十，固請辭事，上嘉其意，許之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi, having reached seventy years of age, firmly requested to resign office; the emperor commended his intent and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi turned seventy he repeatedly asked to retire. The emperor praised his wish and agreed.

sentences.zh: 以為侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，又固讓，上不許。

translations.literal: He was made Palace Attendant, Senior Grandee of the Left, and Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies; he again firmly declined, and the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He was named palace attendant, senior grandee of the left, and grand prefect with honors equal to the three excellencies—but he declined again, and the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 表疏數十上，又面陳曰：「張良名賢，漢高猶許其退，臣有何用，必為聖朝所須。」

translations.literal: He submitted memorials dozens of times, and face to face said: "Zhang Liang was a famed worthy; even Emperor Gaozu of Han permitted his retirement. Of what use am I that the sage dynasty must need me?"
translations.idiomatic: He sent up dozens of memorials and pleaded in person: "Zhang Liang was a celebrated worthy, and even Emperor Gaozu of Han let him withdraw. What use am I that the court must keep me?"

sentences.zh: 乃至稽顙自陳，言輒泣涕。

translations.literal: He even knocked his forehead to the ground pleading his case; whenever he spoke, tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: He went so far as to knock his forehead to the floor in supplication, weeping whenever he spoke.

sentences.zh: 上不能奪，聽以郡公罷就第，月給錢十萬，米百斛，衞史五十人。

translations.literal: The emperor could not override him and permitted him to retire to his mansion as commandery duke, with monthly stipend of one hundred thousand coins, one hundred hu of grain, and fifty guard attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to prevail, the emperor let him retire to his mansion as commandery duke, with a monthly stipend of one hundred thousand cash, one hundred hu of grain, and fifty guard attendants.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，又申前命，復固辭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, the previous appointment was renewed; he again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 457 the earlier appointment was renewed; he declined once more.

sentences.zh: 三年，司空竟陵王誕據廣陵反，復以慶之為使持節、都督南兗徐兗三州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，率眾討之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Prince Dan of Jingling, Minister of Works, rebelled holding Guangling; Qingzhi was again made Bearer of the Staff, Director of military affairs in Southern Yanzhou, Xu, and Yanzhou, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opening of the Office with equal precedence as the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou, leading troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Prince Dan of Jingling, minister of works, rebelled at Guangling. Qingzhi was again made bearer of the staff, director of military affairs in Southern Yanzhou, Xu, and Yanzhou, grand general of chariots and cavalry, grand prefect, and governor of Southern Yanzhou, and sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 至歐陽，誕遣客慶之宗人沈道愍齎書說慶之，餉以玉鐶刀，慶之遣道愍反，數以罪惡。

translations.literal: At Ouyang, Dan sent a client, Qingzhi's clansman Shen Daomin, bearing a letter to persuade Qingzhi, presenting a jade ring-knife as gift; Qingzhi sent Daomin back and enumerated Dan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: At Ouyang, Dan sent a client—Qingzhi's kinsman Shen Daomin—with a letter of persuasion and a jade ring-knife as a gift. Qingzhi sent him back and listed Dan's crimes one by one.

sentences.zh: 慶之至城下，誕登樓謂之曰：「沈君白首之年，何為來？」

translations.literal: When Qingzhi reached the city walls, Dan mounted the tower and said to him: "Master Shen, in the white-haired years of age—why have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi reached the walls, Dan climbed the tower and called down: "Master Shen, at your white-haired age—why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「朝廷以君狂愚，不足勞少壯，故使僕來耳。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "The court considers you mad and foolish—not worth troubling the young and strong—so they sent me."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi answered: "The court thinks you too mad and foolish to waste the young and strong on—so they sent me."

sentences.zh: 上慮誕北奔，使慶之斷其走路。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Dan would flee north and ordered Qingzhi to cut off his escape route.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Dan might flee north, the emperor ordered Qingzhi to block his escape.

sentences.zh: 慶之移營白土，去城十八里。

translations.literal: Qingzhi moved camp to Baitu, eighteen li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi shifted camp to Baitu, eighteen li from the city.

sentences.zh: 又進新亭，誕果出走，不得去，還城，事在誕傳。

translations.literal: He then advanced to Xinting; Dan indeed tried to flee but could not get away and returned to the city—the account is in Dan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced to Xinting. Dan did try to break out but could not get away and returned to the city—the full story is told in Dan's biography.

sentences.zh: 慶之進營洛橋西，焚其東門，值雨不克。

translations.literal: Qingzhi advanced camp west of Luo Bridge and burned the east gate, but rain prevented success.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi moved his camp west of Luo Bridge and burned the east gate, but rain thwarted the assault.

sentences.zh: 慶之兄子僧榮，時為兗州刺史，鎮瑕丘，遣子懷明率數百騎詣受慶之節度。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's nephew Seng Rong, then Governor of Yanzhou garrisoning Xiaqiu, sent his son Huaiming with several hundred horsemen to submit to Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's nephew Seng Rong, then governor of Yanzhou at Xiaqiu, sent his son Huaiming with several hundred horsemen to serve under Qingzhi's command.

sentences.zh: 慶之塞壍，造攻道，立行樓土山，并諸攻具。

translations.literal: Qingzhi filled moats, built assault ramps, erected mobile towers and earthen mounds, and all siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi filled the moats, built assault ramps, raised mobile towers and earthen mounds, and assembled every siege engine.

sentences.zh: 時夏雨，不得攻城，上使御史中丞庾徽之奏免慶之官以激之，詔無所問。

translations.literal: During summer rains siege was impossible; the emperor had Vice Censor-in-Chief Yu Huizhi memorial to dismiss Qingzhi from office to spur him; the edict took no action.
translations.idiomatic: Summer rains made assault impossible. The emperor had vice censor-in-chief Yu Huizhi memorialize to strip Qingzhi of office as a spur—but the edict took no action.

sentences.zh: 誕餉慶之食，提挈者百餘人，出自北門，慶之不問，悉焚之。

translations.literal: Dan sent food to Qingzhi carried by more than a hundred bearers exiting the north gate; Qingzhi gave no acknowledgment and had it all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent provisions to Qingzhi, more than a hundred bearers carrying them out the north gate. Qingzhi ignored the gift and had everything burned.

sentences.zh: 誕於城上授函表，倩慶之為送，慶之曰：「我奉詔討賊，不得為汝送表。

translations.literal: From the wall Dan handed down a sealed memorial and asked Qingzhi to deliver it; Qingzhi said: "I bear orders to suppress the rebel—I cannot carry your memorial for you.
translations.idiomatic: From the wall Dan handed down a sealed petition and asked Qingzhi to deliver it. Qingzhi said: "I have orders to suppress a rebel. I cannot carry your petition.

sentences.zh: 汝必欲歸死朝廷，自應開門遣使，吾為汝送護之。」

translations.literal: If you truly wish to surrender and accept death before the court, you should open the gates and send envoys yourself—I will escort them for you."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish to surrender and accept judgment from the throne, open the gates and send envoys yourself. I will escort them for you."

sentences.zh: 每攻城，輒身先士卒。

translations.literal: Whenever he attacked the city he personally led from the front.
translations.idiomatic: In every assault he placed himself at the head of the troops.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「卿為統任，當令處分有方，何蒙楯城下，身受矢石邪。

translations.literal: The emperor admonished him: "You hold overall command—you should direct affairs with method. Why shield yourself below the walls and personally receive arrows and stones?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warned him: "You hold supreme command. You should direct the battle with discipline. Why crouch beneath the ramparts yourself and take arrows and stones?

sentences.zh: 脫有傷挫，為損不少。」

translations.literal: If you are wounded, the loss would be no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: If you are hurt, the damage will be far from small."

sentences.zh: 自四月至于七月，乃屠城斬誕。

translations.literal: From the fourth month until the seventh, the city was slaughtered and Dan was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month to the seventh the city was taken by storm and Dan was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 進慶之司空，又固讓。

translations.literal: Qingzhi was promoted to Minister of Works; he again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was promoted to minister of works and again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 於是與柳元景並依晉密陵侯鄭袤故事，朝會慶之位次司空，元景在從公之上，給卹吏五十人，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Then he and Liu Yuanjing both followed the Jin precedent of Marquis Mi of Zheng Mao: at court assemblies Qingzhi's seat rank was that of Minister of Works, Yuanjing above attendant dukes; fifty condolence attendants granted; ceremonial horses at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Yuanjing then followed the Jin precedent of Zheng Mao, marquis of Milin: at court Qingzhi was seated in minister-of-works rank and Yuanjing above attendant dukes; each received fifty attendants and ceremonial horses at the gate.

sentences.zh: 四年，西陽五水蠻復為寇，慶之以郡公統諸軍討之，攻戰經年，皆悉平定，獲生口數萬人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Xiyang Wushui tribes raided again; Qingzhi as commandery duke commanded all armies against them; after a year of fighting all was pacified and tens of thousands of captives taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Xiyang Wushui tribes raided again. As commandery duke, Qingzhi commanded the campaign. After a year of fighting all was pacified and tens of thousands of captives were taken.

sentences.zh: 居清明門外，有宅四所，室宇甚麗。

translations.literal: He lived outside Qingming Gate with four residences; their halls and rooms were very splendid.
translations.idiomatic: He lived outside Qingming Gate in four mansions, their halls and chambers sumptuous.

sentences.zh: 又有園舍在婁湖，慶之一夜攜子孫徙居之，以宅還官。

translations.literal: He also had a garden estate at Lou Lake; in one night Qingzhi moved with children and grandchildren to live there and returned the residences to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also owned a garden estate at Lou Lake. In a single night Qingzhi moved his children and grandchildren there and returned the city mansions to the state.

sentences.zh: 悉移親戚中表於婁湖，列門同閈焉。

translations.literal: He moved all kin and cousins to Lou Lake, their gates aligned in the same lane.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated all his kin and cousins to Lou Lake, their gates opening onto the same lane.

sentences.zh: 廣開田園之業，每指地示人曰：「錢盡在此中。」

translations.literal: He greatly expanded agricultural estates; pointing at the land he would show people: "All my money is in here."
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded his farms and estates. Pointing at the land he would tell visitors: "All my wealth is in here."

sentences.zh: 身享大國，家素富厚，產業累萬金，奴僮千計。

translations.literal: He personally enjoyed a great fief; his household had long been rich, assets amounting to tens of thousands in gold, servants numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He personally enjoyed a great fief; his family had long been wealthy, with assets worth tens of thousands in gold and more than a thousand servants.

sentences.zh: 再獻錢千萬，穀萬斛。

translations.literal: He twice presented ten million in cash and ten thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he presented ten million cash and ten thousand hu of grain to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以始興優近，求改封南海郡，不許。

translations.literal: Because Shixing was advantageous and close, he requested change of enfeoffment to Nanhai commandery—not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shixing was rich and close at hand, he asked to be re-enfeoffed in Nanhai commandery. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 妓妾數十人，並美容工藝。

translations.literal: Dozens of singing girls and concubines, all beautiful and skilled in arts.
translations.idiomatic: He kept dozens of concubines and entertainers, all beautiful and accomplished in the arts.

sentences.zh: 慶之優游無事，盡意歡愉，非朝賀不出門。

translations.literal: Qingzhi lived at ease with nothing to do, indulging in pleasure—he did not leave home except for court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi lived in easy leisure, taking his pleasure fully. He left home only for court audiences.

sentences.zh: 每從遊幸及校獵，據鞍陵厲，不異少壯。

translations.literal: Whenever he joined imperial tours or hunts, he sat the saddle fiercely—no different from his youth.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours and hunts he still rode the saddle with fierce vigor, no different from a young man.

sentences.zh: 太子妃上世祖金鏤匕箸及杅杓，上以賜慶之，曰：「卿辛勤匪殊，歡宴宜等，且觴酌之賜，宜以大夫為先也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort presented to Xiaowu gilded spoons, chopsticks, and ladles; the emperor bestowed them on Qingzhi, saying: "Your toil is no different—feasting should be equal; and when it comes to gifts for drinking, the grandee should come first."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort had presented Xiaowu with gilded spoons, chopsticks, and ladles. The emperor gave them to Qingzhi, saying: "Your labors are no less than anyone's; at feast you should enjoy the same honors. When it comes to gifts for the cup, the grandee should come first."

sentences.zh: 上嘗歡飲，普令羣臣賦詩，慶之手不知書，眼不識字，上逼令作詩，慶之曰：「臣不知書，請口授師伯。」

translations.literal: The emperor once at a merry feast ordered all ministers to compose poetry; Qingzhi's hands did not know writing, his eyes did not know characters; the emperor pressed him to compose; Qingzhi said: "Your servant cannot write—please let me dictate to Master Shi."
translations.idiomatic: Once at a merry feast the emperor ordered every minister to compose a poem. Qingzhi could neither write nor read. When pressed, he said: "I cannot write. Let me dictate to Master Yan."

sentences.zh: 上即令顏師伯執筆，慶之口授之曰：「微命值多幸，得逢時運昌。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately had Yan Shibo take brush; Qingzhi dictated: "Humble life met with much fortune, blessed to encounter an age of flourishing fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yan Shibo take brush and ink while Qingzhi dictated: "A humble life has met with great fortune; I have lived in a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 朽老筋力盡，徒步還南崗。

translations.literal: Worn and old, sinews and strength spent—on foot I return to South Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sinews spent and strength gone in old age, I walk back to South Ridge.

sentences.zh: 辭榮此聖世，何媿張子房。」

translations.literal: Resigning glory in this sage age—what shame compared to Zhang Ziliang?"
translations.idiomatic: To yield honor in such a sage reign—what shame need I feel before Zhang Liang?"

sentences.zh: 上甚悅，眾坐稱其辭意之美。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; those seated praised the beauty of his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, and everyone present praised the poem's grace.

sentences.zh: 世祖晏駕，慶之與柳元景等並受顧命，遺詔若有大軍旅及征討，悉使委慶之。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died, Qingzhi with Liu Yuanjing and others all received testamentary charge; the final edict said that for major military affairs and campaigns, all were to be entrusted to Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu died, Qingzhi and Liu Yuanjing and the others received a deathbed charge. The testament decreed that all major armies and campaigns were to be entrusted to Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，加慶之几杖，給三望車一乘。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Former Emperor ascended, Qingzhi was granted folding stool and staff, and one three-canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed former emperor Liu Ziye took the throne, Qingzhi was granted a folding stool and staff and a three-canopy carriage.

sentences.zh: 慶之每朝賀，常乘猪鼻無幰車，左右從者不過三五人。

translations.literal: At each court audience Qingzhi usually rode a pig-snout carriage without canopy; attendants on left and right numbered no more than three or five.
translations.idiomatic: At court audiences he usually rode a plain pig-snout carriage without awning, attended by no more than three or five followers.

sentences.zh: 騎馬履行園田，政一人視馬而已。

translations.literal: Riding a horse through his gardens and fields, only one man tending the horse accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When he rode through his farms, only one groom went with him.

sentences.zh: 每農桑劇月，或時無人，遇之者不知三公也。

translations.literal: In the busiest farming and sericulture months, sometimes no one was with him; those who met him did not know he was one of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the busiest farming and mulberry seasons he sometimes went entirely alone. People who met him on the road never guessed he was one of the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及加三望車，謂人曰：「我每遊履田園，有人時與馬成三，無人則與馬成二。

translations.literal: When the three-canopy carriage was added, he said to people: "Whenever I wandered my fields, with a man it was three with the horse; without a man, two with the horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the three-canopy carriage was granted, he remarked: "When I roam my fields, with a groom it is three counting the horse; without one, two counting the horse.

sentences.zh: 今乘此車，安所之乎。」

translations.literal: Now riding this carriage—where would I go?"
translations.idiomatic: Where am I supposed to go in a carriage like this?"

sentences.zh: 及賜几杖，並固讓。

translations.literal: When the stool and staff were granted, he again firmly declined both.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined both the carriage and the stool and staff.

sentences.zh: 廢帝狂悖無道，眾並勸慶之廢立，及柳元景等連謀，以告慶之。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was mad and lawless; many urged Qingzhi to depose and replace him; Liu Yuanjing and others formed a linked plot and told Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor was violent and lawless. Many urged Qingzhi to depose him. Liu Yuanjing and others formed a conspiracy and confided in Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 慶之與江夏王義恭素不厚，發其事，帝誅義恭、元景等，以慶之為侍中、太尉，封次子中書郎文季建安縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Qingzhi and Prince Yigong of Jiangxia had never been close; he exposed the plot; the emperor executed Yigong, Yuanjing, and others, made Qingzhi Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed his second son Wenji, Secretariat Gentleman, as Marquis of Jian'an with fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi had never been close to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia. He exposed the plot. The emperor executed Yigong, Yuanjing, and the rest, made Qingzhi palace attendant and grand commandant, and enfeoffed his second son Wenji, a secretariat gentleman, as marquis of Jian'an with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 義陽王昶反，慶之從帝度江，總統眾軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Chang of Yiyang rebelled, Qingzhi crossed the river with the emperor and exercised overall command of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chang of Yiyang rebelled, Qingzhi crossed the Yangzi with the emperor and took overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 少子文耀，年十餘歲，善騎射，帝愛之，又封永陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Youngest son Wenyao, just over ten, skilled at riding and archery—the emperor favored him and also enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yongyang with fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Wenyao, barely in his teens and skilled at riding and archery, won the emperor's favor and was also enfeoffed as marquis of Yongyang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 帝凶暴日甚，慶之猶盡言諫爭，帝意稍不說。

translations.literal: The emperor's cruelty grew daily; Qingzhi still spoke fully in remonstrance and debate; the emperor's mood gradually turned displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor grew crueler by the day, Qingzhi still remonstrated without restraint. The emperor's pleasure in him gradually faded.

sentences.zh: 及誅何邁，慮慶之不同，量其必至，乃閉清谿諸橋以絕之。

translations.literal: When He Mai was executed, fearing Qingzhi would not agree, calculating he would surely come, the emperor closed all bridges on Qingxi to cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: After He Mai was executed, fearing Qingzhi would object and guessing he would come to protest, the emperor closed every bridge on the Qingxi to block him.

sentences.zh: 慶之果往，不得度而還。

translations.literal: Qingzhi indeed went but could not cross and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi did come, but unable to cross he turned back.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣慶之從子攸之齎藥賜慶之死，時年八十。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Qingzhi's clansman nephew Youzhi bearing poison to grant Qingzhi death; he was eighty at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Qingzhi's clansman Shen Youzhi with poison to grant him death. Qingzhi was eighty.

sentences.zh: 是年初，慶之夢有人以兩匹絹與之，謂曰：「此絹足度。」

translations.literal: Earlier that year Qingzhi dreamed someone gave him two bolts of silk, saying: "This silk is enough to measure."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier that year Qingzhi dreamed that someone gave him two bolts of silk, saying: "This silk is enough to measure you out."

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「老子今年不免。

translations.literal: He told people: "This old man cannot escape death this year.
translations.idiomatic: He told others: "This old man will not escape death this year.

sentences.zh: 兩匹，八十尺也。

translations.literal: Two bolts—eighty chi.
translations.idiomatic: Two bolts—eighty chi.

sentences.zh: 足度，無盈餘矣。」

translations.literal: Enough to measure—with nothing left over."
translations.idiomatic: Enough to measure me out, with nothing left over."

sentences.zh: 及死，賜與甚厚，追贈侍中，太尉如故，給鸞輅轀輬車，前後羽葆、鼓吹，諡曰忠武公。

translations.literal: At his death, gifts were very generous; posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant as before; given imperial funeral carriage with canopies front and rear, feather banners, and martial music; posthumous title Loyal and Martial Duke.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the gifts were lavish. He was posthumously honored as palace attendant and grand commandant as before, granted an imperial funeral carriage with feather banners and martial music front and rear, and given the posthumous title Loyal and Martial Duke.

sentences.zh: 未及葬，帝敗。

translations.literal: Before burial could take place, the emperor was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could be buried, the emperor was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追贈侍中、司空，諡曰襄公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, posthumous honors were Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; posthumous title Duke Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended, Qingzhi was posthumously honored as palace attendant and minister of works with the posthumous title Duke Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長子文叔，歷中書黃門郎，景和末，為侍中。

translations.literal: Eldest son Wenshu served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate of the Secretariat; at the end of Yuanhe he was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Wenshu had served as gentleman of the yellow gate in the secretariat and, by the end of Yuanhe, was palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 慶之之死也，不肯飲藥，攸之以被揜殺之。

translations.literal: At Qingzhi's death he refused to drink the poison; Youzhi smothered him with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi was ordered to die he refused the poison. Youzhi smothered him with a quilt.

sentences.zh: 文叔密取藥藏錄。

translations.literal: Wenshu secretly took the poison and kept it as a record.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu secretly kept some of the poison as a record.

sentences.zh: 或勸文叔逃避，文叔見帝斷截江夏王義恭支體，慮奔亡之日，帝怒，容致義恭之變，乃飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: Some urged Wenshu to flee; seeing the emperor had dismembered Prince Yigong limb by limb, fearing that if he fled the emperor's rage might bring calamity like Yigong's upon the family, he drank poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Wenshu to flee. But he had seen the emperor hack Prince Yigong limb from limb, and feared that flight would only provoke a slaughter like Yigong's. He drank the poison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 子祕書郎昭明，亦自縊死。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoming, Secretariat Gentleman, also hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoming, a secretariat gentleman, hanged himself as well.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，改封蒼梧郡公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, the enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Cangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 471 the family enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Cangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，還復先封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui, his former fief was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year 1 his original enfeoffment was restored.

sentences.zh: 時改始興為廣興，昭明子曇亮，襲廣興郡公。

translations.literal: At that time Shixing was renamed Guangxing; Tanliang, son of Zhaoming, inherited Duke of Guangxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing was then renamed Guangxing, and Tanliang, son of Zhaoming, succeeded as duke of Guangxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 慶之弟劭之，元嘉中，為廬陵王紹南中郎行參軍，討建安揭陽諸賊，病卒。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's younger brother Shaozhi, in the Yuanjia era, served as acting aide on the staff of the Southern Army of Prince Shao of Luling; he campaigned against the bandits of Jian'an and Jieyang and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's younger brother Shaozhi served in the Yuanjia era as acting staff officer on Prince Shao of Luling's southern army staff, campaigned against bandits in Jian'an and Jieyang, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 兄子僧榮，敞之之子也。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Seng Rong was the son of Changzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Seng Rong was the son of Changzhi.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，為安成相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was Chancellor of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiaojian era he became chancellor of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 荊、江反叛，發兵拒臧質，質遣其安成相臧眇之討僧榮，擊破之。

translations.literal: When Jing and Jiang rebelled, he raised troops to resist Zang Zhi; Zhi sent his Chancellor of Ancheng Zang Miaozhi to attack Seng Rong and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jing and Jiang rebellions he raised troops against Zang Zhi. Zhi sent his Ancheng chancellor Zang Miaozhi against Seng Rong and routed him.

sentences.zh: 大明中，為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he was Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Daming reign he served as inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 景和中，徵為黃門郎，未還，卒。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era he was summoned as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; before he could return, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era he was recalled as gentleman of the yellow gates but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 子懷明，太宗泰始初，居父憂，起為建威將軍，東征南討有功，封吳興縣子，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: His son Huaiming, at the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Ming, was in mourning for his father when he was called up as Establishing Might General; in eastern and southern campaigns he had merit and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuxing with four hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaiming, early in Emperor Ming's Taishi reign, left mourning to become establishing might general. He earned distinction in campaigns east and south and was made viscount of Wuxing with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 歷位黃門侍郎，再為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of Palace Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and twice served as Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace gentleman of the yellow gates and twice governed South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，丁母艱，去職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he entered mourning for his mother and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhui era he resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範為逆，起為冠軍將軍，統水軍防固石頭，朱雀失守，懷明委軍奔走，頃之憂卒。

translations.literal: When Prince Guiyang Xiufan rebelled, Huaiming was called up as Champion General, commanding the navy to defend Shitou; when Zhuque Gate was lost, Huaiming abandoned his army and fled; shortly after he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guiyang Xiufan rebelled, Huaiming was made champion general to hold Shitou with the fleet. After Zhuque Gate fell he abandoned his troops and fled, then died of shame soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 慶之從弟法系字體先，亦有將用。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's younger cousin Faxing, styled Tixian, also had military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's cousin Faxing, courtesy name Tixian, was likewise a capable commander.

sentences.zh: 初為趙伯符將佐，後隨慶之征五水蠻。

translations.literal: At first he was an aide to Zhao Bofu; later he followed Qingzhi in the campaign against the Five Waters Man.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as aide to Zhao Bofu, then followed Qingzhi against the Five Waters tribes.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐逆，以為南中郎參軍，加寧朔將軍，領三千人前發，與柳元景旦至新亭。

translations.literal: When the Shizu campaigned against the usurper, Faxing was made Southern Army Aide, promoted to Pacify-the-North General, and led three thousand men forward; with Liu Yuanjing he reached Xinting at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shizu's campaign against the usurper he became southern army aide and pacify-the-north general, led three thousand men ahead, and reached Xinting at dawn with Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 元景居中營，宗慤居西營，法系居東營。

translations.literal: Yuanjing held the central camp, Zong Que the western camp, and Faxing the eastern camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing took the center, Zong Que the west, and Faxing the east.

sentences.zh: 東營據岡，賊攻元景，法系臨射之，所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: The eastern camp held the hill; when the enemy attacked Yuanjing, Faxing shot down on them and killed very many.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern camp held the heights. When the rebels struck Yuanjing, Faxing rained arrows down and killed a great number.

sentences.zh: 法系塹外樹悉伐之令倒，賊劭來攻，緣樹以進，彭棑多開隙，選善射手，的發無不中，死者交橫。

translations.literal: Faxing had all the trees outside the moat cut down to fall inward; when the enemy Shao came to attack, they advanced along the trees; the stockade had many gaps opened; he chose skilled archers whose aimed shots never missed, and the dead lay crossed in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing felled the trees beyond the ditch so they fell inward. When Shao's men attacked along the trunks, the palisade left wide gaps. He posted crack archers whose every shaft found its mark, and corpses piled up in heaps.

sentences.zh: 事平，以為寧朔將軍、始興太守，討蕭簡於廣州。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was made Pacify-the-North General and Administrator of Shixing and was sent to campaign against Xiao Jian at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was made pacify-the-north general and Shixing administrator and sent to suppress Xiao Jian at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞臺軍將至，簡誑其眾曰：「臺軍是賊劭所遣。」

translations.literal: When he heard the imperial army was coming, Jian deceived his followers, saying, "The court army is sent by the rebel Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the imperial army was approaching, Jian lied to his men: "The court troops are Liu Shao's men.

sentences.zh: 並信之。

translations.literal: They all believed it.
translations.idiomatic: They all believed him.

sentences.zh: 前征北參軍顧邁被賊徙在城內，善天文，云「荊、江有大兵」。

translations.literal: Former Northern Campaigning Aide Gu Mai, whom the rebels had moved inside the city, was skilled in astronomy and said, "Great armies are coming from Jing and Jiang."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Mai, a former northern campaigning aide held inside the city, was skilled in astronomy and declared, "Large armies are coming from Jing and Jiang."

sentences.zh: 城內由此固守。

translations.literal: Because of this those inside the city held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison therefore dug in.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖先遣鄧琬圍簡，唯治一攻道，法系至，曰：「宜四面並攻，若守一道，何時可拔。」

translations.literal: Earlier the Shizu had first sent Deng Wan to besiege Jian, building only one assault ramp; when Faxing arrived he said, "You should attack on all four sides—if you hold to one route, when will the city be taken?
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu had first sent Deng Wan to besiege Jian with only one assault ramp. Faxing said, "Attack from all four sides. One approach alone will never take the city.

sentences.zh: 琬慮功不在己，不從。

translations.literal: Wan feared the credit would not be his and did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, fearing the glory would not be his, refused.

sentences.zh: 法系曰：「更相申五十日。」

translations.literal: Faxing said, "Let us give each other fifty more days."
translations.idiomatic: Faxing said, "Give me fifty more days."

sentences.zh: 日盡又不克，乃從之。

translations.literal: When the days were up and he still had not taken it, Wan then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When the fifty days passed without success, Wan finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 八道俱攻，一日即拔，斬蕭簡，廣州平。

translations.literal: Eight routes attacked together; in one day it was taken, Xiao Jian was beheaded, and Guangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Eight assault columns struck at once. The city fell in a day, Xiao Jian was executed, and Guangzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 封庫藏付鄧琬而還。

translations.literal: He sealed the treasury stores, handed them to Deng Wan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the treasury, handed it to Deng Wan, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 官至驍騎將軍、尋陽太守，新安王子鸞北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: He reached the offices of Valiant Cavalry General, Administrator of Xunyang, and Major of the Northern Army of Prince Ziluan of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to valiant cavalry general, Xunyang administrator, and major on Prince Ziluan of Xin'an's northern army staff.

sentences.zh: 劭之子文秀，別有傳。

translations.literal: Shao's son Wenxiu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's son Wenxiu is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 慶之羣從姻戚，由之在列位者數十人。

translations.literal: Through Qingzhi's clan kin and marriage connections, several tens held rank at court.
translations.idiomatic: Through Qingzhi's kinsmen and marriage alliances, dozens held office at court.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：張釋之云，用法一偏，天下獄皆隨輕重。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Shizhi said that if the application of law is skewed in one direction, prisons throughout the realm will all follow that bias in severity.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zhang Shizhi observed that when the law tilts one way, every prison in the empire tilts with it.

sentences.zh: 縣衡於上，四海共稟其平，法亂於朝，民無所措手足。

translations.literal: When the scales hang level above, the four seas all receive their fairness; when law is chaotic at court, the people have nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: When the scales hang true at the top, the realm shares in their justice; when law collapses at court, the people do not know where to turn.

sentences.zh: 師伯藉寵代臣，勢震朝野，傾意廝臺，情以貨結，自選部至于局曹，莫不從風而靡。

translations.literal: Shibo relied on favor as a minister of the succession, his power shaking court and countryside; he poured his heart into the clerical offices and bound men with gifts—from the Selection Bureau down to the desk bureaus, none failed to bend before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo traded on favor as heir-apparent minister until his power shook court and country. He lavished attention on the clerical offices and bought loyalty with wealth. From the selection bureau to the lowest desk, every office bent to his will.

sentences.zh: 曲徇私請，因停詔敕，天震霣怒，仆者相望，師伯任用無改，而王、謝免職。

translations.literal: He twisted the law for private requests and thereby halted imperial edicts; heaven thundered and rain fell in anger, and the struck-down lay one after another—yet Shibo's appointments went unchanged while Wang and Xie were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He bent the law to private ends and blocked imperial edicts. Heaven itself seemed to thunder in wrath, and the punished fell one after another—yet Shibo kept his posts while Wang and Xie lost theirs.

sentences.zh: 君子謂是舉也，豈徒失政刑而已哉！

translations.literal: Men of discernment said of this affair that it was surely more than a mere failure of government and punishment!
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men judged that this was far more than a failure of law and governance alone!
